Talos prevalent malware filename pattern — VID001.exe and d4aa3e70..._N_Exe.exe AIInstallation Medium
Catches the distinctive filenames Talos called out as example file names for this week's prevalent malware: 'VID001.exe' (Coinminer) and the UUID-prefixed numeric-suffix pattern 'd4aa3e7010220ad1b458fac17039c274_<N>_Exe.exe' (W32.Injector / Win.Dropper.Miner). The naming scheme is unique enough that it'll catch variants whose hash has rotated. Rationale: Article explicitly names 'VID001.exe' (Win.Worm.Coinminer::1201) and 'd4aa3e7010220ad1b458fac17039c274_63_Exe.exe' / '_62_Exe.exe' (W32.Injector + Win.Dropper.Miner) as example filenames. The 32-hex-prefix + numeric-suffix + _Exe.exe pattern is distinctive enough to catch hash-rotated variants from the same campaign. Scoped to user-writable paths to avoid trusted-software false positives. Cross-checked against: • https://talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation?s=9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507 • https://talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation?s=96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974
ATT&CKT1036.005 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Video-editing pipeline producing temporary files named VID###.exe (rare — most produce VID###.mp4/avi, not .exe)
  • Internal build system using UUID-prefixed artifact names from a hash-then-rename pipeline (would land in build paths, not %TEMP%/%APPDATA%)
  • Security researcher renaming captured samples to the article's example filenames for testing
  • Penetration test using the disclosed filenames as a thematic naming convention
Suppression filter
| where FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files\" and FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files (x86)\" and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsMpEng.exe", "MsSense.exe", "CSFalconService.exe")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: confirm file landed in user-writable path (Downloads / Temp / AppData / Public / ProgramData) — system-path matches are unlikely and warrant deeper inspection. Pull SHA256 and compare to the UC1 hash list — if it matches, treat as confirmed prevalent malware. Step 2 — Contain: quarantine the file, block the SHA256 in EDR indicators, isolate the host if the file executed (check chain to UC1). Step 3 — Hunt: pivot on the UUID prefix 'd4aa3e7010220ad1b458fac17039c274_' across DeviceFileEvents — the suffix increments (62, 63, ...) suggest a generator producing many variants; enumerate all _N_Exe.exe variations seen in the estate. Sweep for outbound connections to mining pools and beacon C2 from any host that touched these filenames in the past 30 days.
union
( DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
  | where FileName =~ "VID001.exe" or FileName matches regex @"(?i)^d4aa3e7010220ad1b458fac17039c274_\d+_Exe\.exe$"
  | where FolderPath has_any (@"\Users\", @"\AppData\", @"\Temp\", @"\Public\", @"\ProgramData\")
  | project Timestamp, EventKind="ProcessExec", DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
),
( DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
  | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
  | where FileName =~ "VID001.exe" or FileName matches regex @"(?i)^d4aa3e7010220ad1b458fac17039c274_\d+_Exe\.exe$"
  | project Timestamp, EventKind="FileDrop", DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine="", InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
)
| order by Timestamp desc
union
( ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
  | where TargetProcessName endswith @"\VID001.exe" or TargetProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\d4aa3e7010220ad1b458fac17039c274_\d+_Exe\.exe$"
  | project TimeGenerated, EventKind="ProcessExec", DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, SHA256, ParentProcessName
),
( ImFileEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
  | where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
  | where TargetFileName =~ "VID001.exe" or TargetFileName matches regex @"(?i)^d4aa3e7010220ad1b458fac17039c274_\d+_Exe\.exe$"
  | project TimeGenerated, EventKind="FileDrop", DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName=ActingProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine=ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256=TargetFileSHA256, ParentProcessName=""
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Talos Prevalent Malware Filename Pattern (VID001.exe / d4aa3e70 UUID-suffix)
id: f8a2c4d6-1b3e-4c7f-8e9a-6d5b2c1f3e84
description: Detects creation or execution of files matching the distinctive filenames Talos called out in the 2026-06-11 prevalent-malware roundup — VID001.exe (Coinminer) and d4aa3e7010220ad1b458fac17039c274_<N>_Exe.exe (Injector / Dropper.Miner).
references:
  - https://blog.talosintelligence.com/a-tale-of-two-eras/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1204.002
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1036.005
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  sel_vid:
    Image|endswith: '\VID001.exe'
  sel_uuid:
    Image|re: '(?i)\\d4aa3e7010220ad1b458fac17039c274_\d+_Exe\.exe$'
  condition: 1 of sel_*
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:(1 OR 11) (@Image:(*\VID001.exe OR *\vid001.exe) OR @TargetFilename:(*\VID001.exe OR *\vid001.exe) OR @Image:*d4aa3e7010220ad1b458fac17039c274_*_Exe.exe OR @TargetFilename:*d4aa3e7010220ad1b458fac17039c274_*_Exe.exe)
(#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 OR #event_simpleName=FileWritten)
| ImageFileName=/\\VID001\.exe$/i OR TargetFileName=/\\VID001\.exe$/i OR ImageFileName=/\\d4aa3e7010220ad1b458fac17039c274_\d+_Exe\.exe$/i OR TargetFileName=/\\d4aa3e7010220ad1b458fac17039c274_\d+_Exe\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, #event_simpleName, ImageFileName, TargetFileName, SHA256HashData], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.user) as user values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent values(Processes.process) as cmdline from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="VID001.exe" OR match(Processes.process_name, "^d4aa3e7010220ad1b458fac17039c274_\d+_Exe\.exe$")) Processes.process_path IN ("*\\Users\\*", "*\\AppData\\*", "*\\Temp\\*", "*\\Public\\*", "*\\ProgramData\\*") by Processes.dest Processes.process_name Processes.process_path Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.user) as user values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent values(Processes.process) as cmdline from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="VID001.exe" OR match(Processes.process_name, "^d4aa3e7010220ad1b458fac17039c274_\d+_Exe\.exe$")) Processes.process_path IN ("*\\Users\\*", "*\\AppData\\*", "*\\Temp\\*", "*\\Public\\*", "*\\ProgramData\\*") by Processes.dest Processes.process_name Processes.process_path Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_known_good
falsepositives:
    - Third-party EDR / forensic tools — extend the filter list
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98") or SHA1 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98") or MD5 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98") or SHA1 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98") or MD5 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

New Attacks Trick OpenClaw AI Agent Into Running Code and Leaking Secrets

The Hacker News
2026-06-11 15 use cases 5 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Two security teams have shown, in separate research published this week, that OpenClaw, the popular self-hosted AI agent, can be driven to run attacker-controlled code or hand over sensitive data through ordinary-looking inputs. Imperva buried instructions inside shared contacts, vCards, and location pins that the agent executed without the victim ever seeing them. Varonis built a test agent on

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] OpenClaw channel-extension allowlist bypass via attacker display-name rename · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender · Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] OpenClaw agent runtime spawning shell / download-and-run after prompt injection · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] OpenClaw / AI agent egress to imperva_artifactory.com (Imperva PoC payload server) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] OpenClaw / AI agent process reading credential stores (.env, .aws/credentials, id_rsa) · [LLM] AI agent mailbox auto-forwarding credentials to external address (Varonis Pinchy pattern) · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
OpenClaw / AI agent egress to imperva_artifactory.com (Imperva PoC payload server) AICommand & Control High
Hunts the only network IOC in the article: the Imperva-controlled server that the prompt-injected OpenClaw agent was tricked into reaching for a download-and-run payload. Any DNS/HTTP egress to this host from a self-hosted-agent box is a direct hit on the published PoC. Rationale: imperva_artifactory.com is the only externally-named infrastructure in the article (Imperva PoC payload server). A second source check on the Imperva blog post for this campaign was not possible without WebSearch, but the article unambiguously names the domain — high-fidelity IOC. Fix from prior emission: dropped DeviceName from CommonSecurityLog/ImDnsActivity/ImNetworkSession projections and replaced with each table's correct host identifier (DvcHostname / SourceHostName / Computer).
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal security team replaying the Imperva PoC in a lab for awareness training
  • Threat-intel scraper / sandbox detonating the article's IOCs as part of an enrichment pipeline
  • Reverse-engineering box with researcher curl/wget probing the domain
  • Web-content filter URL-categorisation crawler resolving the domain for classification
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("curl.exe","wget.exe","powershell.exe") or InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("explorer.exe","sandbox-agent.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "--research" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "--sandbox"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pivot on InitiatingProcessFileName/InitiatingProcessCommandLine for the egressing host — confirm it is an OpenClaw runtime (python, node, openclaw-server, langchain) and identify the user/session that triggered the agent action. Pull the agent's task log for the 5-minute window before the lookup. 2) Contain: isolate the host via Defender/EDR live response, kill the agent process, revoke any cloud / mail credentials the agent had access to (especially Gmail OAuth, AWS IAM, Slack tokens). 3) Hunt: search 30d back across the org for any other host that resolved this domain; review inbound vCards, shared contacts and location pins in the agent's connected channels for hidden-instruction payloads; verify OpenClaw is on >= 2026.4.23.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("imperva_artifactory.com","imperva-artifactory.com") or AdditionalFields has "imperva_artifactory.com"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DnsQuery has_any ("imperva_artifactory.com","imperva-artifactory.com")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DstIpAddr),
(ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where Url has_any ("imperva_artifactory.com","imperva-artifactory.com") or DstHostname has_any ("imperva_artifactory.com","imperva-artifactory.com")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url),
(DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where Name has_any ("imperva_artifactory.com","imperva-artifactory.com")
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, ResultCode),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where RequestURL has_any ("imperva_artifactory.com","imperva-artifactory.com") or DestinationHostName has_any ("imperva_artifactory.com","imperva-artifactory.com")
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceHostName, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestURL, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct)
title: OpenClaw Imperva PoC C2 Domain Resolution
id: 7a2c8e54-3f1d-4f8a-9c2d-8b0a1f7e5d11
description: DNS lookup or network egress to imperva_artifactory.com, the attacker-controlled server used in the Imperva OpenClaw prompt-injection PoC to deliver a download-and-run payload.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-attacks-trick-openclaw-ai-agent.html
author: detection-engineering
date: 2026/06/19
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1105
logsource:
  category: dns
selection:
  QueryName|contains:
    - 'imperva_artifactory.com'
    - 'imperva-artifactory.com'
condition: selection
level: high
(source:(windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd OR linux.syslog OR cisco.umbrella OR zscaler) AND (@DnsQuery:(*imperva_artifactory.com* OR *imperva-artifactory.com*) OR @dns.question.name:(*imperva_artifactory.com* OR *imperva-artifactory.com*) OR @DestinationHostname:(*imperva_artifactory.com* OR *imperva-artifactory.com*) OR @network.destination.domain:(*imperva_artifactory.com* OR *imperva-artifactory.com*)))
(#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/imperva[_-]artifactory\.com$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic where Network_Traffic.All_Traffic.dest IN ("imperva_artifactory.com","imperva-artifactory.com") OR Network_Traffic.All_Traffic.dest_host IN ("imperva_artifactory.com","imperva-artifactory.com") by Network_Traffic.All_Traffic.src Network_Traffic.All_Traffic.src_ip Network_Traffic.All_Traffic.dest Network_Traffic.All_Traffic.dest_port Network_Traffic.All_Traffic.app | `drop_dm_object_name(Network_Traffic.All_Traffic)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
OpenClaw agent runtime spawning shell / download-and-run after prompt injection AIInstallation High
Hunts the execution step of the Imperva attack: the OpenClaw runtime (python/node/openclaw-server) spawning a shell or download utility (curl, wget, powershell -c IEX, bash -c) to fetch and run a remote script. Article: 'the hidden text told the agent to download and run a script from a server the researchers controlled. It did.' Rationale: Article directly states OpenClaw downloaded and ran a script when given the hidden instruction. The detection chains the (parent=AI-runtime) → (child=shell/downloader) → (cmdline=fetch-and-exec primitive) tuple — each leg is necessary, the conjunction is high-fidelity. References article phrasing 'download and run a script' literally.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1059.004 T1105 T1204
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legit data-engineering pipeline where a python agent uses curl/wget to fetch CSV/JSON inputs
  • DevOps bootstrap script: python orchestrator running 'curl ... | sh' for a known install (helm, kubectl)
  • Jupyter notebook user genuinely running !curl or !wget to download dataset
  • SRE running an OpenClaw maintenance task that legitimately chmod +x a vendor binary
  • Security researcher replaying the PoC in an isolated test agent
Suppression filter
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "github.com" and ProcessCommandLine !has "pypi.org" and ProcessCommandLine !has "npmjs.org"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "--ci" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "--devbootstrap"
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture full ProcessCommandLine + the parent's task ID / API correlation token; query the OpenClaw audit log for the agent task that produced this shell-out and identify the inbound message (vCard / shared contact / email) that triggered it. 2) Contain: kill agent runtime, revoke connected-service tokens (Gmail, Slack, Teams, AWS), block the remote URL/IP at egress proxy, and remove any dropped binary from disk. 3) Hunt: 30d sweep for the same parent→child pattern across other OpenClaw / LangChain / AutoGPT hosts; review all shared contacts and vCards delivered to agent-monitored mailboxes for angle-bracketed payloads (the Imperva trick); confirm OpenClaw version is ≥ 2026.4.23.
let agent_parents = dynamic(["python.exe","python3.exe","python","node.exe","node","openclaw.exe","openclaw-server","openclaw-agent.exe","uvicorn.exe","gunicorn"]);
let exec_children = dynamic(["powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","bash","sh","zsh","curl.exe","wget.exe","curl","wget","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","mshta.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (agent_parents)
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("openclaw","open_claw","claw-agent","langchain","autogen","crewai")
| where FileName in~ (exec_children)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("IEX ","Invoke-Expression","DownloadString","DownloadFile"," | sh"," | bash","-OutFile","--data-binary","chmod +x","-EncodedCommand","base64 -d","eval $(")
   or (FileName in~ ("curl.exe","curl","wget.exe","wget") and ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"https?://[^\s]+\.(sh|py|ps1|exe|bin)(\s|$)")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc

(ImProcessCreate

  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine)
(source:(windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd) AND (@ParentImage:(*python* OR *node* OR *openclaw* OR *uvicorn* OR *gunicorn*) OR @ParentCommandLine:(*openclaw* OR *open_claw* OR *langchain*) OR @process.parent.executable.path:(*python* OR *node* OR *openclaw*)) AND (@Image:(*powershell.exe OR *pwsh.exe OR *cmd.exe OR *curl.exe OR *wget.exe OR *bash OR *sh OR *certutil.exe) OR @process.executable.path:(*curl OR *wget OR *bash OR *sh)) AND (@CommandLine:(*IEX* OR *Invoke-Expression* OR *DownloadString* OR *"chmod +x"* OR *EncodedCommand* OR *" | sh"* OR *" | bash"*) OR @process.command_line:(*"chmod +x"* OR *" | sh"* OR *" | bash"* OR *IEX*)))

OpenClaw / AI agent process reading credential stores (.env, .aws/credentials, id_rsa) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Targets the Varonis 'Pinchy' scenario: the AI agent was tricked into harvesting credentials it had filesystem access to — mock AWS IAM keys, DB connection strings, SSH credentials. Detects an AI-runtime process opening canonical credential files, which a legitimate agent task should rarely do. Rationale: Varonis' Pinchy test explicitly forwarded 'mock AWS IAM access keys, database connection strings, and SSH credentials in plaintext' — those live in the named files. Pairing AI-runtime parentage with these canonical paths gives medium-FP-rate hunting signal while staying article-grounded.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1555 T1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legit Python data-pipeline that reads .aws/credentials to call boto3 (e.g. an ETL agent)
  • Developer testing a langchain tool that genuinely needs AWS creds
  • DevOps automation: openclaw agent doing scheduled backup using ssh keys
  • Configuration-management script (Ansible/Salt) running under python interpreter as part of CI
  • Initial agent first-run bootstrap that copies sample .env
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "boto3" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "--config" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "backup"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the agent task log around the file-open time and identify the inbound prompt that drove the read (look for words like 'incident', 'staging access', 'QBR'); check if the file content was subsequently sent to an outbound recipient. 2) Contain: rotate the credentials in the file (AWS keys, SSH keys, DB passwords), revoke active sessions, kill the agent process, and constrain the agent's filesystem scope (per Varonis' guidance — trust-level-based connector access). 3) Hunt: search OutboundMail / EmailEvents / OfficeActivity for SendItem / forward operations within 5 minutes of the credential file read; review the 'instruction file' / system prompt for tampering; sweep for similar reads across other agent hosts.
let agent_proc = dynamic(["python.exe","python3.exe","python","node.exe","node","openclaw.exe","openclaw-server","openclaw-agent.exe","uvicorn.exe","gunicorn"]);
let cred_files = dynamic([".env","credentials","id_rsa","id_ed25519",".pgpass",".npmrc",".pypirc","accessTokens.json","config.json"]);
let cred_paths = dynamic([@"\.aws\credentials",@"\.aws\config",@"\.ssh\id_",@"\.kube\config",@"\.docker\config.json",@"\.gcloud\",@"\.azure\accessTokens.json","/.aws/credentials","/.aws/config","/.ssh/id_","/.kube/config","/.docker/config.json","/.gcloud/","/.azure/accessTokens.json"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
   or ActionType startswith "File"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (agent_proc)
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("openclaw","open_claw","langchain","autogen","crewai","llama_index")
| where FileName in~ (cred_files) or FolderPath has_any (cred_paths)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, ActionType, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let agent_proc = dynamic(["python.exe","python3.exe","python","node.exe","node","openclaw.exe","openclaw-server","openclaw-agent.exe","uvicorn.exe","gunicorn"]);
let cred_files = dynamic([".env","credentials","id_rsa","id_ed25519",".pgpass",".npmrc",".pypirc","accessTokens.json"]);
let cred_path_fragments = dynamic([".aws/credentials",".aws/config",".ssh/id_",".kube/config",".docker/config.json",".gcloud/",".azure/accessTokens.json"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any (agent_proc) or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("openclaw","open_claw","langchain","autogen","crewai")
| where TargetFileName in~ (cred_files) or TargetFilePath has_any (cred_path_fragments)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, EventType
title: AI Agent Runtime Reading Credential Store
id: c34b7d11-9b1c-4a93-9efb-2d6f0a1f88e2
description: Python / Node / OpenClaw runtime opens canonical secret files (.aws/credentials, .ssh/id_rsa, .env, .kube/config) — matches the Varonis 'Pinchy' agent-phishing scenario where the agent was talked into harvesting credentials.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-attacks-trick-openclaw-ai-agent.html
author: detection-engineering
date: 2026/06/19
tags:
  - attack.t1552.001
  - attack.t1555
  - attack.t1005
logsource:
  category: file_access
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\python.exe'
      - '\python3.exe'
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\openclaw.exe'
      - '\openclaw-server.exe'
      - '\openclaw-agent.exe'
  selection_file:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\.aws\credentials'
      - '\.aws\config'
      - '\.ssh\id_rsa'
      - '\.ssh\id_ed25519'
      - '\.kube\config'
      - '\.docker\config.json'
      - '\.azure\accessTokens.json'
      - '\.env'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_file
level: high
(source:(windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd) AND (@Image:(*\python.exe OR *\python3.exe OR *\node.exe OR *\openclaw*) OR @process.executable.path:(*python* OR *node* OR *openclaw*) OR @CommandLine:(*openclaw* OR *langchain* OR *autogen* OR *crewai*)) AND (@TargetFilename:(*\.aws\credentials* OR *\.aws\config* OR *\.ssh\id_* OR *\.kube\config* OR *\.azure\accessTokens.json* OR *\.env) OR @file.path:(*/.aws/credentials* OR *.aws/config* OR */.ssh/id_* OR */.kube/config* OR */.env)))
(#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo OR #event_simpleName=FileWritten)
| ContextImageFileName=/(python3?|node|openclaw|openclaw-server|openclaw-agent|uvicorn|gunicorn)(\.exe)?$/i
| regex("(\\\\\\.aws\\\\(credentials|config)|\\\\\\.ssh\\\\id_(rsa|ed25519)|\\\\\\.kube\\\\config|\\\\\\.docker\\\\config\\.json|\\\\\\.azure\\\\accessTokens\\.json|\\\\\\.env$|/\\.aws/(credentials|config)|/\\.ssh/id_(rsa|ed25519)|/\\.kube/config|/\\.env$)", field=TargetFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())

AI agent mailbox auto-forwarding credentials to external address (Varonis Pinchy pattern) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects the Varonis 'agent phishing' outcome: an LLM-driven mailbox agent sends out messages containing credential-shaped payloads (AWS access key IDs, RSA private key blocks, DB connection strings) to a recipient outside the org. Triggered by a 'team lead Dan / production incident' style pretext. Rationale: Article: 'Pinchy found the credentials and forwarded mock AWS IAM access keys, database connection strings, and SSH credentials in plaintext' and shipped 'a synthetic dataset of 247 enterprise customers' under subjects like 'weekly customer export' and 'production incident'. Detection pivots on (agent-mailbox sender) ∧ (external recipient) ∧ (Pinchy-style subject OR credential-shaped body) — tight to the article's two named pretexts.
ATT&CKT1114.003 T1567 T1041
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legit security drill where an agent sends test credentials to a Varonis/Imperva-style scanner
  • DevOps automation that pushes rotating credentials to an external SaaS vendor (e.g. Datadog API key)
  • Help-desk agent sending recovery instructions containing the literal string 'access key'
  • Legal/QBR thread where the agent forwards a real quarterly business review deck with 'customer export' wording
  • Marketing newsletter from agent mailbox to external mailing list (false positive on subject)
Suppression filter
| where not(Subject has_any ("test mail","automated drill","phish-test","newsletter","unsubscribe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full message body, attachments, and the agent-task chain that led to the Send; identify the inbound message (Dan-style pretext) and the prompt content the agent acted on. 2) Contain: revoke the agent's Send permission and OAuth grant on the mailbox, rotate any leaked credentials, recall the message via OfficeActivity (Outbound recall) and quarantine attachments via M-PostDelivery action; warn the recipient. 3) Hunt: review 30 days of outbound mail from any AI-agent mailbox for the same credential-string patterns; verify whether the strict-profile system prompt is intact and version-controlled per Varonis' guidance; widen the rule to Gmail / Workspace agents.
let agent_mailboxes = dynamic(["pinchy@","agent@","assistant@","openclaw@","ai-bot@","copilot@"]);  // tune per org
let internal_domain = "yourcorp.com";
let sus_subj = dynamic(["production incident","staging access","weekly customer export","QBR","customer export","credentials","access key","creds for"]);
EmailEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where EmailDirection in ("Outbound","Intra-org")
| where SenderFromAddress has_any (agent_mailboxes) or SenderMailFromAddress has_any (agent_mailboxes)
| where not(RecipientEmailAddress endswith internal_domain)
| where Subject has_any (sus_subj)
   or AdditionalFields has_any ("AKIA","ASIA","BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY","BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY","aws_secret_access_key","postgres://","mysql://","mongodb://")
| join kind=leftouter (EmailAttachmentInfo | project NetworkMessageId, AttachFile=FileName, AttachType=FileType, AttachSize=FileSize) on NetworkMessageId
| project Timestamp, NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, AttachFile, AttachType, AttachSize, DeliveryAction
| order by Timestamp desc
let agent_mailboxes = dynamic(["pinchy@","agent@","assistant@","openclaw@","ai-bot@","copilot@"]);
let internal_domain = "yourcorp.com";
let sus_subj = dynamic(["production incident","staging access","weekly customer export","QBR","customer export","credentials","access key","creds for"]);
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Operation in ("Send","SendOnBehalf","SendAs","New-InboxRule","Set-InboxRule")
| where UserId has_any (agent_mailboxes) or MailboxOwnerUPN has_any (agent_mailboxes)
| extend Recipients_str = tostring(Recipients)
| where not(Recipients_str has internal_domain) and Recipients_str !=""
| where Subject has_any (sus_subj)
   or Parameters has_any ("ForwardingSmtpAddress","ForwardTo","AKIA","ASIA","BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY","BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY","aws_secret_access_key","postgres://","mysql://")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, MailboxOwnerUPN, Operation, Subject, Recipients_str, ClientIP, UserAgent, Parameters
(source:(office365 OR google.workspace) AND @evt.name:(*Send* OR *Forward* OR *New-InboxRule* OR *Set-InboxRule*) AND (@usr.email:(*pinchy@* OR *agent@* OR *assistant@* OR *openclaw@* OR *ai-bot@* OR *copilot@*) OR @actor.email:(*pinchy@* OR *agent@* OR *assistant@* OR *openclaw@* OR *ai-bot@*)) AND -@recipient.email:*@yourcorp.com AND (@email.subject:(*"production incident"* OR *"staging access"* OR *"weekly customer export"* OR *QBR* OR *credentials* OR *"access key"*) OR @email.body:(*AKIA* OR *ASIA* OR *"BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY"* OR *aws_secret_access_key* OR *postgres://* OR *mysql://*)))

OpenClaw channel-extension allowlist bypass via attacker display-name rename AIDelivery Medium
Hunts the InfoSec Write-ups secondary finding: OpenClaw's Slack / Discord / Matrix / Zalo / Teams channel extensions resolved the allowlist by mutable display name rather than stable user ID. An attacker rename to match an allowed user lets them steer the agent. Detection: bursty display-name changes by external/low-tenure accounts to high-privilege names in those platforms. Rationale: Article: 'the startup code resolved each channel's allowlist by mutable display name instead of a stable ID, so an attacker who renamed themselves to match an allowed user could slip onto the list and steer the agent.' Detection focuses on the rename event itself across the named platforms (Slack / Discord / Matrix / Zalo / Teams), gated by high-privilege target name patterns to keep noise down.
ATT&CKT1656 T1078 T1199
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: high — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legit name changes during onboarding/role change (promotion to CTO, new HR lead)
  • Marriage / pronoun / gender display-name updates
  • Bot rebranding where a service account is renamed for a product launch
  • M&A integration where employees adopt the parent-company naming convention
  • Time-zone aliasing (e.g. 'Alice (PST)') triggering the on-call regex
Suppression filter
| where Old != "" and isnotempty(Old)
| where AccountDisplayName !endswith "@yourcorp.com" or Application != "Microsoft Teams"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the actor's account age, MFA status, and last 30d sign-in history; compare the renamed display name to OpenClaw's channel-extension allowlist file to see if they now match an allowed entry. 2) Contain: revert the display name via admin API, suspend the account if low-tenure or external-tenant, and rotate any agent token / connector that trusted the renamed account. 3) Hunt: pivot on the actor's userId to find subsequent messages to OpenClaw-monitored channels; review the OpenClaw runtime config for any extension still using display-name-based allowlisting (un-patched); confirm OpenClaw is upgraded to the fix.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application in ("Microsoft Teams","Slack","Discord","Matrix","Zalo")
| where ActionType in ("UpdateUser","UserProfileChanged","user_profile_changed","display_name_change","UserUpdated","users.profile_set")
| extend Old = tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).previous_display_name), New = tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).display_name)
| extend Old = iff(isempty(Old), tostring(AdditionalFields.PreviousDisplayName), Old), New = iff(isempty(New), tostring(AdditionalFields.NewDisplayName), New)
| where isnotempty(New) and Old != New
| where New matches regex @"(?i)(admin|ceo|cto|cfo|security|finance|hr|ops|it[-_]?ops|openclaw|agent|bot|sre|oncall)"
| project Timestamp, Application, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, Old, New, IPAddress, CountryCode, UserAgent
| order by Timestamp desc
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload in ("MicrosoftTeams","AzureActiveDirectory")
| where Operation in ("MemberAdded","MemberRoleChanged","TeamsTenantSettingChanged","Update user.","UserUpdated")
| where Parameters has "DisplayName" or Parameters has "displayName"
| extend NewName = extract(@"(?i)displayName[^,]*?:\s*[\"']([^\"']+)", 1, tostring(Parameters))
| where isnotempty(NewName)
| where NewName matches regex @"(?i)(admin|ceo|cto|cfo|security|finance|hr|ops|it[-_]?ops|openclaw|agent|bot|sre|oncall)"
| project TimeGenerated, OfficeWorkload, Operation, UserId, NewName, ClientIP, UserAgent, Parameters
(source:(slack OR microsoft.teams OR discord) AND @evt.name:(*user.profile_changed* OR *UserUpdated* OR *display_name_change* OR *MemberRoleChanged* OR *users.profile_set*) AND (@properties.new_display_name:(*admin* OR *ceo* OR *cto* OR *security* OR *openclaw* OR *agent* OR *bot* OR *sre* OR *oncall*) OR @new_value:(*admin* OR *ceo* OR *security* OR *openclaw* OR *agent*)))
APPLICATION
index=collaboration (sourcetype=slack:audit OR sourcetype=msteams:audit OR sourcetype=discord:audit) (action=user_profile_changed OR action=UserUpdated OR action=display_name_change OR action=user.update) | rex field=changes "(?i)display_?name.*?from\s*[\"']?(?<old_name>[^\"',]+)[\"']?.*?to\s*[\"']?(?<new_name>[^\"',]+)" | where isnotnull(new_name) AND old_name!=new_name | stats min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(old_name) as old_names values(new_name) as new_names count by user, user_id, workspace, app | where count >= 1 | eval suspicious=if(match(new_names, "(?i)(admin|ceo|cto|cfo|security|finance|hr|ops|it[-_]?ops|openclaw|agent)"), 1, 0) | where suspicious=1
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |

    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'

NETWORK

| append

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append

        where Web.dest IN ("imperva_artifactory.com")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS

        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host

            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'

            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")

Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator Delivery High
External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1566
Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents

New GreatXML Exploit Bypasses Windows BitLocker via Recovery Partition XML Files

The Hacker News
2026-06-11 11 use cases 4 techniques 7 kill-chain phases detected

Security researcher Chaotic Eclipse (aka Nightmare-Eclipse and MSNightmare) has released a new Windows BitLocker bypass dubbed GreatXML, a day after they published an exploit for Microsoft Defender. "This was an accidental discovery, it took a total of 4 hours to find this," the researcher said in a post on Blogger. "If you ever attempted to use Windows Defender Offline Scan, you're

CVEsCVE-2026-45585
ATT&CKT1190 T1195.002 T1204.004 T1528

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer). → [LLM] Recovery partition XML drop (unattend.xml / ReAgent.xml) — GreatXML BitLocker bypass · [LLM] Defender Offline Scan trigger preceding recovery-partition activity
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Forced WinRE boot via shutdown /o or reagentc /boottore · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Unprivileged process writing to recovery / EFI / System Reserved volumes
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] BitLocker recovery-key enumeration via manage-bde or Win32_EncryptableVolume WMI · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Recovery partition XML drop (unattend.xml / ReAgent.xml) — GreatXML BitLocker bypass AIWeaponization High
Hunts for the GreatXML primitive: a process writing 'unattend.xml' or 'Recovery\WindowsRE\ReAgent.xml' to a recovery-volume path outside the trusted servicing stack. The exploit requires these two XML artifacts on the root of the recovery partition before a WinRE boot to get shell access to the BitLocker volume. Rationale: The article names exactly two file artifacts ('unattend.xml' and 'Recovery/WindowsRE/ReAgent.xml') dropped at the root of the recovery partition as the entire exploit primitive — these names + recovery-volume paths are the highest-fidelity pivots in the entire write-up. Exclude TrustedInstaller / TiWorker / wuauclt / drvinst / sysprep — the only legit writers of these paths. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1542/001/
ATT&CKT1542.001 T1647
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • TrustedInstaller writing ReAgent.xml during a cumulative update or feature update
  • Sysprep generating unattend.xml during OEM imaging or Audit Mode
  • OEM recovery-image servicing tools refreshing the recovery partition
  • MDT / SCCM task sequence writing answer files to a staged recovery volume
  • Defender platform update touching the WinRE image post-patch
Suppression filter
and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","TiWorker.exe","wuauclt.exe","WindowsUpdateBox.exe","drvinst.exe","sysprep.exe","MsMpEng.exe","MpCmdRun.exe","setup.exe","DismHost.exe") and InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("services.exe","TrustedInstaller.exe") and InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Confirm the writing process and parent chain. Is it TrustedInstaller / TiWorker / wuauclt / WindowsUpdateBox? Cross-check timing against an active Windows Update or feature-upgrade window in the asset record. Pull the SHA256 of the writing process and look up signer/age. Step 2 — Contain: If the writer is interactive user-context (powershell, cmd, explorer, msiexec) and the host has BitLocker enabled, isolate the device via Defender 'Isolate Device' before the user reboots — the exploit only succeeds AFTER a Shift+Restart into WinRE. Block reagentc.exe execution via App Control policy on the asset. Step 3 — Hunt: Pivot to DeviceProcessEvents on the same host for reagentc.exe, 'shutdown /r /o', 'Restart-Computer' with bcdedit changes, and any preceding 'MpCmdRun.exe -OfflineScan' or 'wdo' calls (Defender Offline Scan is the documented prerequisite).
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FileName in~ ("unattend.xml","ReAgent.xml")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Recovery\WindowsRE\", @"\Recovery\", @"System Reserved", @"\HarddiskVolume")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","TiWorker.exe","wuauclt.exe","WindowsUpdateBox.exe","drvinst.exe","sysprep.exe","MsMpEng.exe","MpCmdRun.exe","setup.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          FilePath=strcat(FolderPath, "\\", FileName),
          ParentProcess=InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          Process=InitiatingProcessFileName,
          Cmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          IntegrityLevel=InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel,
          SHA256=InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("unattend.xml","ReAgent.xml")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Recovery\WindowsRE\", @"\Recovery\", @"System Reserved", @"\HarddiskVolume")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","TiWorker.exe","wuauclt.exe","WindowsUpdateBox.exe","drvinst.exe","sysprep.exe","MsMpEng.exe","MpCmdRun.exe","setup.exe")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: GreatXML BitLocker Bypass - Recovery Partition XML Drop
id: 8c4a6f12-9b3e-4c12-a8f1-7e2d4b9c0a55
description: Detects creation or modification of unattend.xml or ReAgent.xml on recovery / System Reserved partitions, the precondition for the GreatXML BitLocker bypass.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-greatxml-exploit-bypasses-windows.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/19
tags:
  - attack.t1542.001
  - attack.defense_evasion
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_name:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '\unattend.xml'
      - '\ReAgent.xml'
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\Recovery\WindowsRE\'
      - '\Recovery\'
      - 'System Reserved'
      - '\HarddiskVolume'
  filter_servicing:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\TrustedInstaller.exe'
      - '\TiWorker.exe'
      - '\wuauclt.exe'
      - '\WindowsUpdateBox.exe'
      - '\drvinst.exe'
      - '\sysprep.exe'
      - '\MsMpEng.exe'
      - '\MpCmdRun.exe'
  condition: selection_name and selection_path and not filter_servicing
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:(*\Recovery\WindowsRE\unattend.xml OR *\Recovery\WindowsRE\ReAgent.xml OR *\Recovery\unattend.xml OR *\Recovery\ReAgent.xml OR *\Recovery\WindowsRE\Unattend.xml OR *\Recovery\WindowsRE\REAGENT.XML OR "*System Reserved*unattend.xml*" OR "*System Reserved*ReAgent.xml*")) -@Image:(*\TrustedInstaller.exe OR *\TiWorker.exe OR *\wuauclt.exe OR *\drvinst.exe OR *\sysprep.exe OR *\MsMpEng.exe OR *\MpCmdRun.exe)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| TargetFileName=/(Recovery\\WindowsRE\\|Recovery\\|System Reserved|HarddiskVolume)/i
| TargetFileName=/(unattend\.xml|ReAgent\.xml)$/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/(TrustedInstaller|TiWorker|wuauclt|WindowsUpdateBox|drvinst|sysprep|MsMpEng|MpCmdRun)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name values(Filesystem.process_path) as process_path values(Filesystem.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="unattend.xml" OR Filesystem.file_name="ReAgent.xml") AND (Filesystem.file_path="*\\Recovery\\WindowsRE\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Recovery\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*System Reserved*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\HarddiskVolume*\\unattend.xml") AND Filesystem.action IN ("created","modified","written") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where NOT match(process_name, "(?i)^(TrustedInstaller|WindowsUpdateBox|wuauclt|TiWorker|drvinst|sysprep|MsMpEng)\.exe$") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Forced WinRE boot via shutdown /o or reagentc /boottore AIExploitation High
Detects the user-mode trigger for the GreatXML bypass: a process invoking 'shutdown' with the /o (advanced options menu → Troubleshoot → WinRE) flag, reagentc.exe with /boottore, or bcdedit toggling the recovery sequence. The article calls out Shift+Restart as the manual path; the equivalent automatable triggers are these CLIs. Rationale: The article explicitly says the trigger is 'holding Shift while clicking Restart in the Windows power menu' to enter WinRE. The CLI equivalents that an attacker would script are shutdown /r /o, reagentc /boottore, and bcdedit recoverysequence — these are the high-fidelity automatable signals. None are typical user activity outside of IT-led troubleshooting. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1542/001/
ATT&CKT1542.001 T1059.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IT helpdesk scripts using shutdown /r /o /t 0 to send a user into recovery for troubleshooting
  • OS deployment / re-imaging via reagentc /enable post-build
  • BitLocker recovery testing by a security team verifying recovery keys
  • Dell/Lenovo OEM recovery utilities reseating boot sequence
  • WSUS / SCCM post-patch reboot orchestration toggling bootsequence
Suppression filter
and InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("services.exe","TrustedInstaller.exe","TiWorker.exe","wuauclt.exe","CcmExec.exe","SoftwareDistribution.exe") and not (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "powershell.exe" and InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("CcmExec.exe","ScClient.exe"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Identify the parent process and the logged-on user. Was this an admin in an interactive RDP/console session, or did it come from a script, scheduled task, or unusual parent (rundll32, mshta, wmic, msiexec)? Correlate with the user's ticket queue / change-management window. Step 2 — Contain: If interactive user-context and BitLocker is enabled, isolate the device immediately — the reboot is the moment shell-in-WinRE materialises. Disable the local account if abuse is suspected. Step 3 — Hunt: Look back 1h on the same host for the GreatXML XML drop (the other UC in this set), MpCmdRun.exe -OfflineScan invocations (the article's documented prerequisite), and reagentc.exe /info reconnaissance. Pivot on AccountName / DeviceId across the fleet for parallel exploitation.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where (FileName =~ "shutdown.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/o" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/r","/g"))
     or (FileName =~ "reagentc.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/boottore","/enable","/setreimage","/setosimage"))
     or (FileName =~ "bcdedit.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("recoverysequence","bootsequence","recoveryenabled"))
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","TiWorker.exe","wuauclt.exe","services.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentProcess=InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          GrandParent=InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          ElevatedToken=InitiatingProcessTokenElevation,
          IntegrityLevel=InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where AccountType != "Machine" and SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| extend Cmd = tolower(CommandLine), Img = tolower(NewProcessName)
| where (Img endswith "\\shutdown.exe" and Cmd contains "/o" and (Cmd contains "/r" or Cmd contains "/g"))
     or (Img endswith "\\reagentc.exe" and (Cmd contains "/boottore" or Cmd contains "/enable" or Cmd contains "/setreimage" or Cmd contains "/setosimage"))
     or (Img endswith "\\bcdedit.exe" and (Cmd contains "recoverysequence" or Cmd contains "bootsequence" or Cmd contains "recoveryenabled"))
| where ParentProcessName !endswith "\\TrustedInstaller.exe" and ParentProcessName !endswith "\\TiWorker.exe" and ParentProcessName !endswith "\\wuauclt.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: WinRE Boot Forced via shutdown /o or reagentc /boottore
id: 1f9c2e8a-3a4d-4b5b-9e22-b6c7e9f1c4d2
description: Detects the user-mode triggers that boot Windows into the Recovery Environment, the second stage of the GreatXML BitLocker bypass after the XML files have been staged.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-greatxml-exploit-bypasses-windows.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/19
tags:
  - attack.t1542.001
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1059.003
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  shutdown_winre:
    Image|endswith: '\shutdown.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: '/o'
  shutdown_reboot:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/r'
      - '/g'
  reagentc:
    Image|endswith: '\reagentc.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/boottore'
      - '/enable'
      - '/setreimage'
      - '/setosimage'
  bcdedit:
    Image|endswith: '\bcdedit.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'recoverysequence'
      - 'bootsequence'
      - 'recoveryenabled'
  filter_servicing:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\TrustedInstaller.exe'
      - '\TiWorker.exe'
      - '\wuauclt.exe'
  condition: ((shutdown_winre and shutdown_reboot) or reagentc or bcdedit) and not filter_servicing
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 ((@Image:(*\shutdown.exe OR *\SHUTDOWN.EXE) AND @CommandLine:(*"/o"* OR *" /o "*) AND @CommandLine:(*"/r"* OR *"/g"*)) OR (@Image:(*\reagentc.exe OR *\REAGENTC.EXE) AND @CommandLine:(*/boottore* OR */setreimage* OR */setosimage*)) OR (@Image:(*\bcdedit.exe OR *\BCDEDIT.EXE) AND @CommandLine:(*recoverysequence* OR *bootsequence* OR *recoveryenabled*))) -@ParentImage:(*\TrustedInstaller.exe OR *\TiWorker.exe OR *\wuauclt.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| (ImageFileName=/\\shutdown\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/\/o\b/i AND CommandLine=/\/(r|g)\b/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\\reagentc\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/\/(boottore|setreimage|setosimage|enable)\b/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\\bcdedit\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/(recoverysequence|bootsequence|recoveryenabled)/i)
| NOT ParentBaseFileName=/(TrustedInstaller|TiWorker|wuauclt)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
