| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.parent_process) as parent_process from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="shutdown.exe" OR Processes.process_name="reagentc.exe" OR Processes.process_name="bcdedit.exe") AND ((Processes.process_name="shutdown.exe" AND Processes.process="*/o*" AND Processes.process="*/r*") OR (Processes.process_name="reagentc.exe" AND Processes.process IN ("*/boottore*","*/enable*","*/setreimage*")) OR (Processes.process_name="bcdedit.exe" AND (Processes.process="*recoverysequence*" OR Processes.process="*bootsequence*" OR Processes.process="*/set*{current}*recoveryenabled*Yes*"))) AND NOT (Processes.user="*$" OR Processes.parent_process_name IN ("TrustedInstaller.exe","TiWorker.exe","wuauclt.exe")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.parent_process) as parent_process from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="shutdown.exe" OR Processes.process_name="reagentc.exe" OR Processes.process_name="bcdedit.exe") AND ((Processes.process_name="shutdown.exe" AND Processes.process="*/o*" AND Processes.process="*/r*") OR (Processes.process_name="reagentc.exe" AND Processes.process IN ("*/boottore*","*/enable*","*/setreimage*")) OR (Processes.process_name="bcdedit.exe" AND (Processes.process="*recoverysequence*" OR Processes.process="*bootsequence*" OR Processes.process="*/set*{current}*recoveryenabled*Yes*"))) AND NOT (Processes.user="*$" OR Processes.parent_process_name IN ("TrustedInstaller.exe","TiWorker.exe","wuauclt.exe")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Defender Offline Scan trigger preceding recovery-partition activity AIWeaponization Medium
Hunts for the GreatXML prerequisite the researcher named explicitly: 'Windows Defender Offline Scan' must have been initiated to make the host vulnerable. Surfaces MpCmdRun.exe -wdo / -OfflineScan or PowerShell Start-MpWDOScan calls — alone (hunting), or chained within 24h to a recovery-partition write / WinRE-boot trigger (alerting). Rationale: The researcher quote is explicit: 'If Defender offline scan was never initiated then you have to either login and initiate it yourself...' — Defender Offline Scan is the documented precondition. MpCmdRun.exe -wdo / -OfflineScan / Start-MpWDOScan are the only ways to trigger it programmatically. Cross-host correlation with recovery-XML drops within 24h is the strongest pivot. Cross-checked against: • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/threat-protection/microsoft-defender-antivirus/command-line-arguments-microsoft-defender-antivirus • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1542/001/
ATT&CKT1562.001 T1542.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • SOC analyst manually triggering an offline scan to remediate a sticky infection
  • SCCM / Intune anti-malware policy scheduling Defender Offline Scans
  • Helpdesk script invoking MpCmdRun.exe -wdo as standard cleanup
  • MSP RMM tooling kicking off offline scans across managed endpoints
  • User running Windows Security UI 'Microsoft Defender Offline scan' button
Suppression filter
and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("CcmExec.exe","ScClient.exe","MsSense.exe","SenseIR.exe","MsMpEng.exe")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Check whether the MpCmdRun.exe / Start-MpWDOScan call has a legitimate parent (MMC, Defender service, SCCM agent). Confirm whether the user is an admin and whether there's an open helpdesk ticket. Step 2 — Contain: Standalone, this is hunting-tier — no immediate isolation. If the joined query fires (offline scan + recovery-XML write within 24h on the same host), isolate the device and revoke BitLocker recovery keys for that volume in Azure AD / on-prem AD. Step 3 — Hunt: Pivot on AccountName fleet-wide for the same offline-scan call pattern in the last 72h — a campaign would touch multiple hosts. Look for reagentc.exe /info, manage-bde -protectors, and bcdedit /enum recovery from the same user.
let OfflineScan = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where (FileName =~ "MpCmdRun.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-wdo","-OfflineScan","OfflineScanList"))
         or (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has "Start-MpWDOScan")
    | project OfflineScanTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName,
              OfflineScanCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
              OfflineScanParent = InitiatingProcessFileName;
let RecoveryWrite = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName in~ ("unattend.xml","ReAgent.xml")
    | where FolderPath has_any (@"\Recovery\", @"System Reserved", @"\HarddiskVolume")
    | project FileWriteTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, FilePath = strcat(FolderPath, "\\", FileName),
              FileWriter = InitiatingProcessFileName;
OfflineScan
| join kind=inner RecoveryWrite on DeviceId
| where FileWriteTime between (OfflineScanTime .. OfflineScanTime + 24h)
| extend DelayMinutes = datetime_diff('minute', FileWriteTime, OfflineScanTime)
| project OfflineScanTime, FileWriteTime, DelayMinutes, DeviceName, AccountName,
          OfflineScanCmd, OfflineScanParent, FilePath, FileWriter
| order by FileWriteTime desc
let OfflineScan = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where (ActingProcessName =~ "MpCmdRun.exe" and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("-wdo","-OfflineScan","OfflineScanList"))
         or (ActingProcessName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ActingProcessCommandLine has "Start-MpWDOScan")
    | project OfflineScanTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, OfflineScanCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine;
let RecoveryWrite = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where TargetFileName in~ ("unattend.xml","ReAgent.xml")
    | where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Recovery\", @"System Reserved", @"\HarddiskVolume")
    | project FileWriteTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, FileWriter = ActingProcessName;
OfflineScan
| join kind=inner RecoveryWrite on DvcHostname
| where FileWriteTime between (OfflineScanTime .. OfflineScanTime + 24h)
| extend DelayMinutes = datetime_diff('minute', FileWriteTime, OfflineScanTime)
| project OfflineScanTime, FileWriteTime, DelayMinutes, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, OfflineScanCmd, TargetFilePath, FileWriter
| order by FileWriteTime desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 ((@Image:(*\MpCmdRun.exe OR *\MPCMDRUN.EXE) AND @CommandLine:(*"-wdo"* OR *"-OfflineScan"* OR *OfflineScanList*)) OR (@Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\PWSH.EXE) AND @CommandLine:*Start-MpWDOScan*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| (ImageFileName=/\\MpCmdRun\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/(\-wdo|\-OfflineScan|OfflineScanList)/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/Start-MpWDOScan/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT

| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="MpCmdRun.exe" AND (Processes.process="*-wdo*" OR Processes.process="*-OfflineScan*" OR Processes.process="*OfflineScanList*")) OR (Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") AND Processes.process="*Start-MpWDOScan*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

BitLocker recovery-key enumeration via manage-bde or Win32_EncryptableVolume WMI AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects reconnaissance against BitLocker protectors and recovery keys — the prerequisite an attacker performs once they have shell access to plan persistence or capture the recovery password. Covers manage-bde.exe with -protectors / recovery / suspend / status, and WMI queries against Win32_EncryptableVolume / Win32_BitLockerStatus. Rationale: Bypassing BitLocker logically demands key/protector access — the article describes shell access to the BitLocker volume. manage-bde -protectors -get and Win32_EncryptableVolume.GetKeyProtectors are the canonical post-shell discovery steps. Reagentc /info confirms which WinRE image is active. The article's primary value is the bypass; the post-bypass enumeration is the high-confidence pivot. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/004/ • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/manage-bde-protectors
ATT&CKT1552.004 T1047 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IT helpdesk running manage-bde -status during user-reported boot issues
  • MEM/Intune client invoking BitLocker cmdlets to verify compliance
  • Backup software (Veeam, Acronis) suspending BitLocker for image snapshot
  • GPO-driven BitLocker key escrow scripts (Get-BitLockerVolume → AD escrow)
  • OS upgrade routines suspending and resuming BitLocker around feature update
Suppression filter
and InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("services.exe","CcmExec.exe","MsSense.exe","WindowsAzureGuestAgent.exe","IntuneManagementExtension.exe","veeam.backup.shell.exe") and not (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "powershell.exe" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "Get-BitLockerVolume" and InitiatingProcessParentFileName =~ "CcmExec.exe")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Confirm parent process — if it's MMC, MEM/Intune client, CcmExec, services.exe, this is likely BAU. If it's user-interactive cmd / powershell / explorer with no ticket, escalate. Pull the user's recent process tree for context. Step 2 — Contain: If the account is non-IT and BitLocker is suspended or recovery key dumped, immediately isolate the host, rotate the BitLocker recovery password (manage-bde -protectors -delete and re-add), and force user re-authentication. Step 3 — Hunt: Across the fleet, search the same user / SID for the recovery-XML drop UC and the WinRE-boot trigger UC — these three together are the full GreatXML chain. Check Azure AD / on-prem AD for unauthorized reads of msFVE-RecoveryInformation objects.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where (FileName =~ "manage-bde.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-protectors","recovery","-suspend","-status","-forcerecovery","-off"))
     or (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Win32_EncryptableVolume","Get-BitLockerVolume","GetKeyProtectors","Win32_BitLockerStatus","Suspend-BitLocker"))
     or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Win32_EncryptableVolume","Win32_BitLockerStatus"))
     or (FileName =~ "reagentc.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/info")
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("services.exe","CcmExec.exe","MsSense.exe","WindowsAzureGuestAgent.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentProcess=InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          IntegrityLevel=InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| extend Cmd = tolower(CommandLine), Img = tolower(NewProcessName)
| where (Img endswith "\\manage-bde.exe" and (Cmd contains "-protectors" or Cmd contains "recovery" or Cmd contains "-suspend" or Cmd contains "-status" or Cmd contains "-forcerecovery" or Cmd contains "-off"))
     or (Img endswith "\\powershell.exe" or Img endswith "\\pwsh.exe") and (Cmd contains "win32_encryptablevolume" or Cmd contains "get-bitlockervolume" or Cmd contains "getkeyprotectors" or Cmd contains "win32_bitlockerstatus" or Cmd contains "suspend-bitlocker")
     or (Img endswith "\\wmic.exe" and (Cmd contains "win32_encryptablevolume" or Cmd contains "win32_bitlockerstatus"))
     or (Img endswith "\\reagentc.exe" and Cmd contains "/info")
| where ParentProcessName !endswith "\\services.exe" and ParentProcessName !endswith "\\CcmExec.exe" and ParentProcessName !endswith "\\MsSense.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Unprivileged process writing to recovery / EFI / System Reserved volumes AIInstallation Medium
Broader complement to the unattend.xml / ReAgent.xml UC — catches any file write into a recovery / boot / EFI partition by a process that isn't the trusted Windows servicing stack. Designed to surface unknown GreatXML variants and pre-OS boot tampering generally, including .xml, .cmd, .bat, .exe, and .efi drops to those volumes. Rationale: The article frames Recovery-Partition XML files as the entry point but explicitly leaves room for variants ('I'm unsure if you can still trigger the bug without...'). A broader file-write hunt over recovery / EFI / System Reserved paths catches future variants and the BIOS-boot-record / EFI-bootkit class of attacks T1542 broadly covers. Allowlist of Windows servicing binaries keeps signal usable. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1542/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1542/003/
ATT&CKT1542 T1542.001 T1542.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Dell SupportAssist / Lenovo Vantage refreshing the OEM recovery partition
  • Macrium / Veeam / Acronis backup writing recovery images
  • Windows feature-update generation 2 servicing during in-place upgrade
  • BCD repair tools (Easy BCD, Windows Repair) modifying EFI
  • WinPE / MDT task sequence staging files before reimage
Suppression filter
and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("SupportAssistAgent.exe","DellSupportAssistRemedy.exe","LenovoVantageService.exe","veeam.backup.shell.exe","acronis_pcbackup.exe","Reflect.exe","DSSvc.exe") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files\Dell\" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files\Lenovo\"
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Group results by InitiatingProcessFileName + DeviceName. Investigate any binary you don't recognise — pull SHA256 and signer. Multi-host writes from a single binary in a short window = campaign. Step 2 — Contain: For interactive/unsigned writers, isolate the host before next reboot. Block the binary fleet-wide via Defender AV custom IOC if confirmed malicious. Step 3 — Hunt: Pivot on the writer's SHA256 across DeviceProcessEvents for parent chain. Look for subsequent reagentc /enable, bcdedit /enum, or shutdown /r /o on the same hosts. Check Azure AD / on-prem for BitLocker key reads.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Recovery\", "System Reserved", @"\EFI\", @"\HarddiskVolume")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","TiWorker.exe","wuauclt.exe","WindowsUpdateBox.exe","drvinst.exe","sysprep.exe","MsMpEng.exe","MpCmdRun.exe","setup.exe","DismHost.exe","dism.exe","smss.exe","wininit.exe","System","svchost.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| extend FileExt = tolower(tostring(split(FileName, ".")[-1]))
| summarize FileCount = count(),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            Files = make_set(FileName, 25),
            Paths = make_set(FolderPath, 25)
            by DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName,
               InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Recovery\", "System Reserved", @"\EFI\", @"\HarddiskVolume")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","TiWorker.exe","wuauclt.exe","WindowsUpdateBox.exe","drvinst.exe","sysprep.exe","MsMpEng.exe","MpCmdRun.exe","setup.exe","DismHost.exe","dism.exe","smss.exe","wininit.exe","svchost.exe")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| summarize FileCount = count(),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            Files = make_set(TargetFileName, 25),
            Paths = make_set(TargetFilePath, 25)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName
| order by FirstSeen desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\Recovery\* OR "*System Reserved*" OR *\EFI\* OR *\HarddiskVolume*) -@Image:(*\TrustedInstaller.exe OR *\TiWorker.exe OR *\wuauclt.exe OR *\WindowsUpdateBox.exe OR *\drvinst.exe OR *\sysprep.exe OR *\MsMpEng.exe OR *\MpCmdRun.exe OR *\setup.exe OR *\DismHost.exe OR *\dism.exe OR *\smss.exe OR *\wininit.exe OR *\svchost.exe)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| TargetFileName=/(\\Recovery\\|System Reserved|\\EFI\\|\\HarddiskVolume)/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/(TrustedInstaller|TiWorker|wuauclt|WindowsUpdateBox|drvinst|sysprep|MsMpEng|MpCmdRun|setup|DismHost|dism|smss|wininit|svchost)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_name) as file_name values(Filesystem.user) as user values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*\\Recovery\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*System Reserved*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\EFI\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\HarddiskVolume*" OR Filesystem.file_path="\\Device\\HarddiskVolume*") AND Filesystem.action IN ("created","modified","written","renamed") AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("TrustedInstaller.exe","TiWorker.exe","wuauclt.exe","WindowsUpdateBox.exe","drvinst.exe","sysprep.exe","MsMpEng.exe","MpCmdRun.exe","setup.exe","DismHost.exe","dism.exe","smss.exe","wininit.exe","System") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where NOT match(user, "(?i).*\$$") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_name) as file_name values(Filesystem.user) as user values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*\\Recovery\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*System Reserved*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\EFI\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\HarddiskVolume*" OR Filesystem.file_path="\\Device\\HarddiskVolume*") AND Filesystem.action IN ("created","modified","written","renamed") AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("TrustedInstaller.exe","TiWorker.exe","wuauclt.exe","WindowsUpdateBox.exe","drvinst.exe","sysprep.exe","MsMpEng.exe","MpCmdRun.exe","setup.exe","DismHost.exe","dism.exe","smss.exe","wininit.exe","System") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where NOT match(user, "(?i).*\$$") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45585")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45585")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium

CodeIgniter4 ext_in bypass: multipart upload with image/* Content-Type but .php/.phar filename AIDelivery High
Hunts the exact bypass condition described in CVE-2026-48062: HTTP POST upload requests where the multipart form-data declares an image MIME type (image/gif, image/jpeg, image/png) while the original client filename carries an executable PHP extension (.php, .phar, .phtml, .phps, .pht). This is the validator's blind spot — ext_in trusts the MIME-derived guessed extension while the attacker keeps the executable filename for $file->move(). Rationale: Anchored on the article's explicit example: `mime_in[avatar,image/gif]|ext_in[avatar,gif]` validator combo passes when uploaded MIME maps to gif but the filename remains .php. Combination of image/* Content-Type + .php-family filename in a single POST is the single highest-fidelity signature of the bypass — legitimate uploads almost never present this pair.
ATT&CKT1190 T1036.008 T1505.003
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Penetration testers running CodeIgniter4 PoC scripts against staging/QA
  • Security scanners (Burp, Nuclei) probing upload endpoints with hybrid payloads
  • Misconfigured legacy CMS plugins that accept double-extension files like backup.php.jpg
  • Researchers re-uploading public CVE-2026-48062 PoC payloads
Suppression filter
| where not (HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent has_any ("Nessus","Qualys","Burp","Nuclei","sqlmap") and Url has_any ("/staging/","/qa/","/test/"))
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: Pull the full request body and headers for the matched POST. Confirm the Content-Type is image/* AND the multipart filename ends .php/.phar/.phtml. Identify the destination application — is it CodeIgniter4 < 4.7.3? Check the response code: 200/302 = upload likely accepted, 4xx = blocked. 2. CONTAIN: If the upload returned 200/302, immediately list the target upload directory (commonly /public/uploads/ or /writable/uploads/) for the dropped file. Quarantine by chmod-ing the directory to deny execute (Apache: AddHandler default-handler .php in .htaccess; nginx: location block returning 403 for *.php). Block the source IP at WAF. 3. HUNT: Pivot on the source IP across all web logs for the prior 30 days — look for reconnaissance against /index.php/users, /index.php/profile, or any CodeIgniter route. Search file events for any .php files created under the upload path by the web user. If a webshell was dropped, treat the host as compromised and begin DFIR.

| where FileMimeType startswith "image/"
| where FileName matches regex @"(?i)\.(php|phar|phtml|phps|pht)$"
| extend LikelyUploadEndpoint = Url has_any (UploadEndpointHints)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, Url, HttpMethod, FileName, FileMimeType,
          HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, HttpStatusCode, LikelyUploadEndpoint, DstHostname
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Web server process writes PHP/PHAR file to public-rooted CodeIgniter upload directory AIInstallation High
Hunts the post-bypass file drop: a PHP/web-server process (php-fpm, w3wp, httpd, nginx, php-cgi) creates a file with a PHP-executable extension under a web-accessible directory. The CodeIgniter4 advisory explicitly warns this happens when uploads use $file->move($path) with the original filename in writable/uploads or public/. Rationale: Article names the exact dangerous combination: $file->move($path) preserving original filename, into a 'web-accessible directory' that 'allow[s] PHP or other executable files to run'. The advisory's recommended workaround — save under writable/uploads instead — tells us legitimate apps SHOULDN'T be writing into public-rooted dirs. Detection pairs the web-tier process identity with PHP extension + public path, all named explicitly in the advisory.
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • WordPress / Drupal / Joomla plugin auto-installer writing PHP under uploads (extremely common — needs allow-list)
  • Legitimate CMS file manager modules where admins upload PHP themes
  • CI/CD deployment to web root via php-fpm-backed admin tool
  • CodeIgniter4 cache file generation writing .php cache fragments (system path, not uploads)
  • Custom in-house web admin panel that legitimately accepts .phtml templates
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("wp-cron","wordpress","composer","deploy","phpunit")) | where not (FolderPath has_any ("\\wp-content\\uploads\\cache\\","\\writable\\cache\\","\\storage\\framework\\"))
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: Pull the file SHA256 + content. Open the first ~512 bytes — webshells almost always start with `<?php` and contain eval()/system()/passthru()/`base64_decode(`. Check FileSize: webshells are typically 200B–8KB; legitimate WordPress plugin files are usually 5KB+ with header comments. Cross-reference InitiatingProcessAccountName against the expected web user (www-data, apache, IUSR). 2. CONTAIN: Remove execute permission on the file (`chmod 600` on Linux, deny PHP handler on Windows). If the file body confirms webshell content, isolate the host from network and snapshot for DFIR. Block source IP at WAF and rotate any DB/API creds stored in the app config. 3. HUNT: Search DeviceProcessEvents for the next 24h on the host for cmd.exe/bash/sh/whoami/net.exe spawned by the web process (UC3 covers this). Search W3CIISLog/NGINX access logs for GET requests to the dropped filename — that's the attacker invoking the webshell. Check for outbound C2 from the web server SHA-pivoted on the

PHP/web process spawns OS shell or recon binary post-upload (webshell execution) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects the execution stage of a successful CVE-2026-48062 exploitation: a web server / PHP-FPM process spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh, or common recon binaries (whoami, net, wmic, systeminfo, ipconfig, curl, wget, certutil). This is the smoking-gun behaviour of a working webshell drop in a CodeIgniter4 upload directory. Rationale: Article explicitly says the bypass 'may lead to arbitrary code execution' via PHP files run from the upload dir. The parent→child pivot from php-fpm/w3wp/httpd to cmd/bash/whoami is the highest-signal expression of that arbitrary code execution. Pairing parent web-process with shell/recon child is the BluRaven 'process-tree' pattern applied to the article's stated outcome.
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1059.001 T1059.003 T1059.004 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • PHP apps using shell_exec() / exec() for legitimate image processing (ImageMagick `convert` wrappers)
  • phpMyAdmin or Webmin invoking system commands from the web tier
  • CI/CD admin tools that run deployment shells from a web UI (Jenkins agent, Rundeck)
  • Custom monitoring dashboards that exec `uname`/`hostname` for system info
  • Drupal/WordPress plugins shelling out to ffmpeg or imagemagick for media conversion
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("convert -","imagemagick","ffmpeg","identify -","composer install","php artisan")) | where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("phpmyadmin","webmin","cpanel"))
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: Pull the full ProcessCommandLine. Look for classic webshell signatures: `cmd /c whoami`, `powershell -nop -w hidden -enc`, `bash -i >& /dev/tcp/`, `id;uname -a;ls`. Cross-reference against the host's expected PHP apps — if it's a CodeIgniter4 < 4.7.3 deployment, correlation with UC1/UC2 is near-conclusive. 2. CONTAIN: Kill the child process. Isolate the web host from network. Disable PHP execution in upload directories (httpd: `<FilesMatch \.ph(p|tml|ar)$> Require all denied </FilesMatch>` in uploads/; nginx: location ~ \.ph(p|tml|ar)$ { return 403; }). Patch CodeIgniter4 to ≥4.7.3. 3. HUNT: Find the dropped webshell file: search DeviceFileEvents for .php/.phar files created by the web process in the last 48h (UC2 query). Pull recent web access logs and look for GET/POST to the dropped filename — that's the attacker's interaction. Hunt for outbound network from the host to anomalous IPs in the same window. Check for newly-created users, scheduled tasks, or SUID binaries.

HTTP GET request to PHP/PHAR file inside CodeIgniter upload directory (webshell invocation) AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts the third stage of CVE-2026-48062 exploitation: an HTTP GET (or POST) request from a public source to a .php/.phar/.phtml file living inside an /uploads/ path. Whether the server returns 200 (executed/served) or anything else, requesting an attacker-controlled PHP path under uploads is itself a high-fidelity indicator of webshell interaction or vulnerability probing. Rationale: Article's workaround section pinpoints that uploads under web root + PHP execution = RCE. A request to `/uploads/<anything>.php` has no legitimate purpose in the default CodeIgniter4 app shape — the framework serves dynamic content through index.php, not via uploaded user PHP. This URI pattern is the attacker's `GET /uploads/shell.php?cmd=whoami` invocation.
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1190 T1071.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Vulnerability scanners (Nessus/Qualys/Burp/Nuclei) probing for webshells
  • Bug bounty researchers testing for CVE-2026-48062
  • Misconfigured CMS where /uploads/ legitimately hosts plugin PHP (uncommon for CodeIgniter)
  • Internal QA team validating patch by attempting the upload
  • Search engine crawlers indexing leaked PHP source
Suppression filter
| where not (UA has_any ("Nessus","Qualys","Burp","Nuclei","sqlmap","acunetix","nikto","masscan","zgrab"))
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: Pull the request: source IP, User-Agent, full URL incl. query string. Look for command-execution patterns in querystring: `?cmd=`, `?c=`, `?exec=`, `?0=`, `?_=`. Check the response status — 200 + non-zero body length = the server processed it. Cross-reference the requested filename against UC2 results: was that exact path created by a web process recently? 2. CONTAIN: If the file exists in the upload dir, delete it. Reconfigure the web server to deny PHP execution under /uploads/ (Apache .htaccess `php_flag engine off`; nginx `location ~ /uploads/ { location ~ \.php$ { return 403; } }`). Block source IP. Patch CodeIgniter4 to ≥4.7.3. 3. HUNT: Pivot on source IP across all web logs — were they probing other CVE-2026-48062-style upload endpoints? Check outbound network for reverse shell from the host post-request (UC3 covers shell spawn). Audit `git log` of the application repo for recent ext_in usage in validation rules — those are the attackable endpoints.
// Requests to PHP under uploads dir — webshell invocation or CVE-2026-48062 follow-up probe
(union isfuzzy=true
    (W3CIISLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where csUriStem matches regex @"(?i)/(public/|writable/)?uploads?/[^?\s]+\.(php|phar|phtml|phps|pht)$"
        | project TimeGenerated, src = cIP, Url = csUriStem, Query = csUriQuery, Method = csMethod,
                  Status = scStatus, UA = csUserAgent, Host = sSiteName),
    (ImWebSession
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where Url matches regex @"(?i)/(public/|writable/)?uploads?/[^?\s]+\.(php|phar|phtml|phps|pht)(\?|$)"
        | project TimeGenerated, src = SrcIpAddr, Url, Query = "", Method = HttpMethod,
                  Status = HttpStatusCode, UA = HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, Host = DstHostname))
| summarize Hits = count(), Files = make_set(Url, 20), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Statuses = make_set(Status, 5)
            by src, UA, Host
| where Hits >= 1
| order by LastSeen desc

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

level: medium

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

    - attack.t1204.002

logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:

level: high

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")

      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",

| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68") or SHA1 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68") or MD5 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68") or SHA1 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68") or MD5 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — npm v12 delivers one of the biggest security improvements in years
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Node/npm/yarn spawning shell or LOLBIN child during package install (postinstall hook abuse) · [LLM] Shai-Hulud npm worm file artifacts written during install (setup_bun.js / bun_environment.js / .truffler-cache) · [LLM] node-gyp implicit rebuild via binding.gyp spawning unexpected non-build child processes · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] TruffleHog binary execution from .truffler-cache (Shai-Hulud post-install credential harvest) · [LLM] Nx s1ngularity exfiltration: public GitHub repo named 's1ngularity-repository' or results.b64 commit · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
Node/npm/yarn spawning shell or LOLBIN child during package install (postinstall hook abuse) AIInstallation Medium
Hunts for npm/yarn/pnpm/bun invoking shells, scripting hosts, or download utilities during the preinstall/install/postinstall lifecycle — the exact code path that Nx s1ngularity, Shai-Hulud, axios hijack, and Mini Shai-Hulud all rode in on. Article-specific because it pivots on the lifecycle-script execution npm v12 is now blocking by default. Rationale: Article explicitly names the preinstall/install/postinstall lifecycle scripts and 'npm install' as the abused vector (code blocks 1-3). Nx s1ngularity ran telemetry.js as postinstall; Mini Shai-Hulud abused preinstall; axios hijacked the postinstall hook. Cross-checked with Sysdig and Datadog Security Labs writeups confirming node→shell child chain. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/shai-hulud-the-novel-self-replicating-worm-infecting-hundreds-of-npm-packages • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/learnings-from-recent-npm-compromises/ • https://www.kodemsecurity.com/resources/vulnerability-alert-s1ngularity-malicious-nx-npm-packages
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.001 T1059.004 T1059.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • node-gyp rebuild legitimately spawning cmd.exe/sh during native module compilation
  • prebuild-install / cmake-js downloading prebuilt binaries via curl
  • Husky/lint-staged pre-commit hooks invoking shells
  • Electron-builder running platform setup scripts
  • CI/CD images calling curl to fetch internal artifact-store deps
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("node-gyp","prebuild-install","cmake-js","electron-builder","husky","lint-staged") and ProcessCommandLine !has_any ("http://","https://","-EncodedCommand","IEX","Invoke-Expression","base64"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: inspect ChildCmd for downloader patterns (curl/wget URLs, base64 blobs, Bun-installer references) and identify the originating package by reading the parent npm install command line and the current cwd / node_modules path. Step 2 — Contain: isolate the developer endpoint, revoke any npm token, GitHub PAT, SSH key, and cloud credential reachable from that user's profile, and force-rotate before they're abused. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot on the SHA256 of the dropped binary across the fleet, search EmailEvents for the developer receiving phishing for their npm account, and check GitHub audit log for new public repos under that user's account (s1ngularity-repository pattern) and for unusual package publishes.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","bun.exe","node","npm","yarn","pnpm","bun")
     or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","npm i ","npm ci","yarn install","yarn add","pnpm install","pnpm add","bun install","bun add")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","sh.exe","bash.exe","sh","bash","dash","zsh","curl.exe","wget.exe","curl","wget","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("node-gyp rebuild","prebuild-install","cmake-js")
            and FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","sh.exe","bash"))   // strip the legit native-build shellouts
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          ChildSHA256 = SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)[\\/](node|npm|yarn|pnpm|bun)(\.exe)?$"
     or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","yarn install","pnpm install","bun install","npm ci")
| where TargetProcessName matches regex @"(?i)[\\/](powershell|pwsh|cmd|wscript|cscript|mshta|sh|bash|dash|zsh|curl|wget|bitsadmin|certutil)(\.exe)?$"
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentCmd = ParentProcessCommandLine,
          ParentImage = ParentProcessName,
          ChildImage = TargetProcessName,
          ChildCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildSha256 = SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Shai-Hulud npm worm file artifacts written during install (setup_bun.js / bun_environment.js / .truffler-cache) AIInstallation High
Detects the distinctive file drops the Shai-Hulud and Mini Shai-Hulud npm worms create during preinstall/postinstall — setup_bun.js, bun_environment.js, bun_installer.js, environment_source.js — plus the ~/.truffler-cache directory used to stage TruffleHog. Article explicitly names Bun-runtime install and TruffleHog as the campaign signatures. Rationale: Article names 'telemetry.js' (Nx s1ngularity), 'Bun runtime install', and 'TruffleHog' as the specific campaign artifacts. External sources (Sysdig, Datadog Security Labs, Upwind, Kodem) confirm setup_bun.js, bun_environment.js, ~/.truffler-cache, and results.b64 as the on-disk signatures of these worms — high-fidelity static IoCs. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/shai-hulud-the-novel-self-replicating-worm-infecting-hundreds-of-npm-packages • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/shai-hulud-2.0-npm-worm/ • https://www.upwind.io/feed/shai-hulud-2-npm-supply-chain-worm-attack • https://www.kodemsecurity.com/resources/vulnerability-alert-s1ngularity-malicious-nx-npm-packages
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer intentionally installing the official Bun runtime via setup_bun script
  • Researcher analysing the Shai-Hulud worm in a sandbox VM also in fleet telemetry
  • Test fixtures intentionally named telemetry.js inside a vendored node_modules
  • Internal package legitimately ships a file named telemetry.js (unusual but possible)
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: identify the parent npm install command and the offending node_modules package directory; capture the package name + version and the SHA256 of the dropped artifact. Step 2 — Contain: take the host off the network, revoke every credential reachable from the developer's home directory (npm token in ~/.npmrc, GitHub PATs in ~/.config, SSH keys in ~/.ssh, cloud creds in ~/.aws, ~/.config/gcloud, browser keyrings), and rotate. Step 3 — Hunt: enumerate all other endpoints that installed the same package version via DeviceFileEvents on SHA256, query GitHub for new public repos in the user's account matching 's1ngularity-repository' or auto-named exfil drops, and review npm publish audit log for any package this developer maintains.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where (FileName in~ ("setup_bun.js","bun_environment.js","bun_installer.js","environment_source.js","telemetry.js")
         and FolderPath has_any (@"\node_modules\", "/node_modules/"))
     or FolderPath has ".truffler-cache"
     or FileName =~ "results.b64"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","bun.exe","node","npm","yarn","pnpm","bun")
     or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","yarn install","pnpm install","bun install","npm ci")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (TargetFileName in~ ("setup_bun.js","bun_environment.js","bun_installer.js","environment_source.js","telemetry.js")
         and TargetFilePath has_any (@"\node_modules\", "/node_modules/"))
     or TargetFilePath has ".truffler-cache"
     or TargetFileName =~ "results.b64"
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)[\\/](node|npm|yarn|pnpm|bun)(\.exe)?$"
     or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","yarn install","pnpm install","bun install","npm ci")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

TruffleHog binary execution from .truffler-cache (Shai-Hulud post-install credential harvest) AIActions on Objectives High
Surfaces execution of TruffleHog from the .truffler-cache staging directory the Shai-Hulud worm chain uses to scan developer file systems for secrets. TruffleHog has no business running on a regular developer endpoint outside of CI scanning workflows. Rationale: Article names 'TruffleHog' explicitly as the credential-scraping tool the Shai-Hulud worm runs. External sources (Sysdig, Datadog Security Labs, Upwind) confirm the binary is cached at ~/.truffler-cache and invoked with filesystem-scan args. Developer endpoints almost never need TruffleHog locally — the binary's presence outside CI is itself the signal. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/shai-hulud-the-novel-self-replicating-worm-infecting-hundreds-of-npm-packages • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/shai-hulud-2.0-npm-worm/ • https://www.upwind.io/feed/shai-hulud-2-npm-supply-chain-worm-attack
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1555 T1083
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • AppSec / security team running TruffleHog locally during a manual audit
  • CI runner endpoint also onboarded to EDR running pre-merge secret scans
  • Developer experimenting with TruffleHog after reading about Shai-Hulud
  • Internal developer training environment intentionally demoing the worm
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("jenkins","gitlab-runner","actions-runner","buildkite") or DeviceName matches regex "(?i)(ci|jenkins|runner|build)")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: confirm the parent process (node/npm/bun chain ⇒ malicious; security-team shell ⇒ benign), and capture the binary SHA256 to compare against official TruffleHog releases. Step 2 — Contain: isolate host, revoke every credential the user has access to (npm, GitHub PAT, SSH, cloud, browser keyring), and assume secrets are already exfiltrated — rotate before they're used. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot on the parent npm install command line to identify the poisoned package + version, sweep DeviceFileEvents fleet-wide for ~/.truffler-cache and setup_bun.js, search GitHub for new public repos in the user's namespace with results.b64 commits, and review the user's recent npm publishes for downstream worm propagation.
let LookbackDays = 14d;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where FileName in~ ("trufflehog","trufflehog.exe")
     or FolderPath has ".truffler-cache"
     or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("trufflehog filesystem","trufflehog git",".truffler-cache")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          Image       = FolderPath,
          Cmd         = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 14d;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where TargetProcessName matches regex @"(?i)[\\/]trufflehog(\.exe)?$"
     or TargetProcessName contains ".truffler-cache"
     or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("trufflehog filesystem","trufflehog git",".truffler-cache")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentImage = ParentProcessName,
          ParentCmd   = ParentProcessCommandLine,
          Image       = TargetProcessName,
          Cmd         = ActingProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
