id: 9f1c5e22-3a7d-4f44-8e91-2f4a8b9c0d11
description: Detects the FireAnt Metakit Vietnamese stock-investment platform spawning script interpreters, LOLBins, or binaries from temp/AppData. ESET attributes a compromised-update-server supply-chain attack (Oct 2025 - Mar 2026) on this product to OceanLotus / APT32 that resulted in SPECTRALVIPER deployment.
references:
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/oceanlotus-external-espionage-domestic-targeting/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/17
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  parent:
    ParentImage|contains:
      - 'FireAnt'
      - 'Metakit'
  suspicious_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\regsvr32.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\wget.exe'
      - '\msiexec.exe'
  suspicious_path:
    Image|contains:
      - '\AppData\Local\Temp\'
      - '\AppData\Roaming\'
      - '\ProgramData\'
      - '\Windows\Temp\'
      - '\Users\Public\'
  condition: parent and (suspicious_child or suspicious_path)
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) @EventID:(1 OR 4688) (@ParentImage:(*FireAnt* OR *fireant* OR *Metakit* OR *metakit*) OR @ParentCommandLine:(*FireAnt* OR *fireant* OR *Metakit*)) (@Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\cmd.exe OR *\wscript.exe OR *\cscript.exe OR *\mshta.exe OR *\rundll32.exe OR *\regsvr32.exe OR *\certutil.exe OR *\bitsadmin.exe OR *\curl.exe OR *\wget.exe OR *\msiexec.exe) OR @Image:(*\AppData\Local\Temp\* OR *\AppData\Roaming\* OR *\ProgramData\* OR *\Windows\Temp\* OR *\Users\Public\*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/fireant|metakit/i OR ParentImageFileName=/(FireAnt|Metakit)/i
| (ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|cmd|wscript|cscript|mshta|rundll32|regsvr32|certutil|bitsadmin|curl|wget|msiexec)\.exe$/i OR regex("\\\\(AppData\\\\Local\\\\Temp|AppData\\\\Roaming|ProgramData|Windows\\\\Temp|Users\\\\Public)\\\\", field=ImageFileName))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name="*fireant*" OR Processes.parent_process="*FireAnt*" OR Processes.parent_process="*Metakit*") AND (Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe") OR Processes.process_path IN ("*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*","*\\AppData\\Roaming\\*","*\\ProgramData\\*","*\\Windows\\Temp\\*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_path Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name="*fireant*" OR Processes.parent_process="*FireAnt*" OR Processes.parent_process="*Metakit*") AND (Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe") OR Processes.process_path IN ("*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*","*\\AppData\\Roaming\\*","*\\ProgramData\\*","*\\Windows\\Temp\\*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_path Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
First-seen connection to recently-registered SPECTRALVIPER-shape C2 domain AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts for any internal host making a first-time HTTPS connection to a domain matching the SPECTRALVIPER C&C naming pattern ESET catalogued (single-word .com domains posing as services - finance/cyber/sync/design themed), where the domain is unseen across the org's 30-day baseline. Designed to catch the next OceanLotus C2 rotation before the IOC list updates. Rationale: Uses the explicit six SPECTRALVIPER C&C domains from ESET Table 2 AND a baseline anti-join so any first-time-in-org connection to a similarly-shaped domain (finance/cyber/services themed single-word .coms — the OceanLotus naming convention) gets flagged. Catches IOC rotation that won't be in the next ESET update.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568 T1583.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Marketing/finance department visiting a newly-launched legitimate fintech site for the first time
  • User clicking a phishing-link analysis service that proxies through similar-shape domains
  • Threat-intel browser extension fetching from a sandbox URL
  • Internal CI/CD reaching a newly-provisioned vendor SaaS subdomain
  • Domain typosquats of legitimate companies (separate detection class)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msedge.exe","chrome.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","iexplore.exe","safari.exe","opera.exe")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: enrich the matched domain with WHOIS / registration date and passive DNS - any domain registered in the last 90 days with low passive-DNS history and matching the SPECTRALVIPER naming theme is high-suspicion; check InitiatingProcessFileName to see whether it's a browser (often FP) or an unsigned binary (almost always TP). 2) CONTAIN: if non-browser process or unsigned binary, isolate the host, sinkhole the domain via DNS RPZ, and block at proxy/firewall; if browser, push the URL to your secure-browsing/SWG block-list pending vendor categorization. 3) HUNT: across the fleet, search the last 90 days for any prior connection to the same domain or any of the six known SPECTRALVIPER C&Cs; pivot on the matched host for any of the 20 SHA1 SPECTRALVIPER hashes and for FireAnt Metakit install activity.
let BaselineDomains = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp between (ago(30d) .. ago(1d))
    | where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
    | extend Domain = tolower(tostring(split(RemoteUrl, "/")[2]))
    | summarize HostCount = dcount(DeviceId) by Domain
    | where HostCount > 2;
let ioc_pattern = @"(?i)(financemachinelearning|gatewayrvcenter|coachcybersecurity|mxprodesign|power-sync-services|leadingfilipinoteams)\.com$";
let shape_pattern = @"(?i)\b(finance|cyber|sync|design|machinelearning|filipino|gateway|rvcenter|prodesign|services|teams)\b";
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend Domain = tolower(tostring(split(RemoteUrl, "/")[2]))
| where Domain matches regex ioc_pattern or Domain matches regex shape_pattern
| join kind=leftanti BaselineDomains on Domain
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, Domain, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let BaselineDomains = ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(30d) .. ago(1d))
    | summarize HostCount = dcount(SrcIpAddr) by DnsQuery=tolower(DnsQuery)
    | where HostCount > 2;
let ioc_known = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com","gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
let shape_pattern = @"(?i)\b(finance|cyber|sync|design|machinelearning|filipino|gateway|rvcenter|prodesign|services|teams)\b";
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| extend DnsQueryLower = tolower(DnsQuery)
| where DnsQueryLower has_any (ioc_known) or DnsQueryLower matches regex shape_pattern
| join kind=leftanti BaselineDomains on $left.DnsQueryLower == $right.DnsQuery
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.defender) @EventID:22 (@QueryName:(*financemachinelearning.com OR *gatewayrvcenter.com OR *coachcybersecurity.com OR *mxprodesign.com OR *power-sync-services.com OR *leadingfilipinoteams.com))
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest
| DomainName=/(financemachinelearning|gatewayrvcenter|coachcybersecurity|mxprodesign|power-sync-services|leadingfilipinoteams)\.com$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName, FirstIP4Record], function=count(), function=min(@timestamp))
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where DNS.query IN ("*financemachinelearning.com","*gatewayrvcenter.com","*coachcybersecurity.com","*mxprodesign.com","*power-sync-services.com","*leadingfilipinoteams.com") OR DNS.query="*" by DNS.src DNS.query | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | join type=left query [ | tstats summariesonly=true earliest(_time) as firstSeenOrg from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where earliest=-30d@d latest=-1d@d by DNS.query | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` ] | where isnull(firstSeenOrg) AND (match(query,"(?i)(finance|cyber|sync|design|machinelearning|filipino|gateway|rvcenter|prodesign).*\.com$")) | sort 0 -count
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where DNS.query IN ("*financemachinelearning.com","*gatewayrvcenter.com","*coachcybersecurity.com","*mxprodesign.com","*power-sync-services.com","*leadingfilipinoteams.com") OR DNS.query="*" by DNS.src DNS.query | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | join type=left query [ | tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) as firstSeenOrg from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where earliest=-30d@d latest=-1d@d by DNS.query | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` ] | where isnull(firstSeenOrg) AND (match(query,"(?i)(finance|cyber|sync|design|machinelearning|filipino|gateway|rvcenter|prodesign).*\.com$")) | sort 0 -count
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("139.162.11.152", "142.91.98.77", "139.180.128.42", "139.99.33.239", "166.88.77.186", "103.119.47.104", "38.60.245.37", "194.68.26.241") or RemoteUrl has_any ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["139.162.11.152", "142.91.98.77", "139.180.128.42", "139.99.33.239", "166.88.77.186", "103.119.47.104", "38.60.245.37", "194.68.26.241"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match
level: critical
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("139.162.11.152", "142.91.98.77", "139.180.128.42", "139.99.33.239", "166.88.77.186", "103.119.47.104", "38.60.245.37", "194.68.26.241")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("139.162.11.152", "142.91.98.77", "139.180.128.42", "139.99.33.239", "166.88.77.186", "103.119.47.104", "38.60.245.37", "194.68.26.241")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries Command & Control Medium
Long subdomain labels + frequent queries to a single 2LD = DNS C2/exfil.
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1048.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemotePort == 53 and isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend qlen = strlen(RemoteUrl)
| where qlen > 50
| extend SecondLevelDomain = extract(@"([\w-]+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,})$", 1, RemoteUrl)
| summarize qcount = count(), uniqueSubs = dcount(RemoteUrl), maxLabel = max(qlen)
    by DeviceName, SecondLevelDomain
| where qcount > 100 and uniqueSubs > 20
| order by qcount desc
// ASIM ImDnsActivity normalises Windows DNS, Sysmon EID 22, Linux dnsmasq, etc.
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where DnsQueryTypeName == "TXT"
| summarize Queries = count(), DistinctNames = dcount(DnsQuery)
            by SrcIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where Queries > 200    // tune to TXT-query baseline for environment
| order by Queries desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard Installation High
ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.
ATT&CKT1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe")
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\atera_agent.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\SplashtopStreamer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\RustDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\NinjaOne.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Remote-Management (RMM) Tool Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0c
status: experimental
description: |
    AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera / Splashtop /
    RustDesk — RMM tools attackers commonly install for hands-on-
    keyboard access. Filter against the IT estate's known tool.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1219/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1219
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\AnyDesk.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer_Service.exe'
            - '\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe'
            - '\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe'
            - '\atera_agent.exe'
            - '\SplashtopStreamer.exe'
            - '\RustDesk.exe'
            - '\NinjaOne.exe'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - IT-approved RMM in use across the estate. Maintain a known-IT-
      tool exclusion list per environment.
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["D511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39F", "59A8553A4F8130F576AB234E0B220BE4D4DA0E98", "9CA1A5C7F79882DB913534C1E62B26BCDCB9F6DD", "A8E2BBBFCB86500322D2367744FA12755AB0C165", "F74F1FEB62B662CDA489FDB2453727824E55ACB9", "F8F8209987CA7F139DE6A62F9E6EE21BD2AE93A9", "19A69F856EFA811C376F68E4FEB0997B4724F8BD", "490194E9BB5128ECA8693AD9E610891C2ED185AF", "51176139B0B2220B802C1578A4994DF68DF5BCD1", "91F042F59BE4BDCB6E5EA21B91DECD731C175B54", "A177ED0BFFEB1EFE1D9D31D72A82EF2625AE646D", "B7B2D2DB544F9EEA74453CDF2B8BEEA58CF07C48", "4AD36AD6C165B5174967020CB1A3358F78D7A283", "57352B3CEEE32216E5AA20BAA848483D7AB5A6FB", "9BC06DF9F932746A05EE728C8B103BD3BA6BF395", "865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "41CB8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B0", "0037DBB0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D20", "5D6194BB48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918B", "B028E947150764A71DEEF498DE6F8C95ECCCB445"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: File or Process Matching Article Hash IOCs
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0b
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__HASH_LIST__` placeholder with article-specific SHA256
    values. Use a watchlist or external indicator file for management
    at scale.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Hashes|contains:
            - 'SHA256=__HASH_PLACEHOLDER_REPLACE_ME__'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive hash match
level: critical
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

CISA KEV: CVE-2026-10520 — Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Vulnerability

CISA KEV
2026-06-11 1 use case 1 technique 2 kill-chain phases detected

Ivanti Sentry (formerly known as MobileIron Sentry) contains an OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution. This vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable. The use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors. Vendor: Ivanti, Product: Sentry. Federal patch due: 2026-06-14.

Vulnerable Baileys (WhatsApp Web) npm package installed (CVE-2026-48063) AIWeaponization Medium
Surfaces endpoints with a Baileys library installed on disk by detecting writes to node_modules/baileys/ or node_modules/@whiskeysockets/baileys/ package.json. Used as asset discovery for the protocolMessage / placeholderResendMessage spoofing vulnerability so vuln-mgmt can pivot to a version check. Rationale: Anchors on the two affected package paths named in the GHSA (`npm:baileys`, `npm:@whiskeysockets/baileys`) and the CVE ID. File-event approach gives coverage on endpoints that aren't in Defender TVM; the Sentinel side uses TVM if available. Source verification: the GHSA itself plus the patch commit 3beb08e on WhiskeySockets/Baileys. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/WhiskeySockets/Baileys/commit/3beb08eecfcb4e65722e674034bd84fb11a9de35 • https://osv.dev/vulnerability/MAL-2026-2153
ATT&CKT1195.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: high — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer workstations doing `npm install` of legitimate Node.js apps that depend on Baileys (e.g. chatbot, WhatsApp gateway projects)
  • CI/CD build agents resolving node_modules during pipeline runs
  • Containerised app builds where the host writes to a mounted node_modules volume
  • Internal company chatbots already running a patched Baileys >=6.7.22 or >=7.0.0-rc12 (version not visible in the file-event path — must be confirmed by reading package.json)
  • Test scaffolding / scratch repos cloned to %TEMP% for vulnerability research
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("npm.exe", "npm-cli.js", "yarn.exe", "pnpm.exe", "node.exe")  // narrow to non-package-manager writes if you want only post-deploy tampering; remove this line for asset-discovery use
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the package.json contents from the host (live response / Run Script) and read the `"version"` field. If the version is < 6.7.22 or in 7.0.0-rc.1 .. 7.0.0-rc11, host is vulnerable. Identify which application owns the node_modules tree (parent directory of node_modules) and the business owner. Step 2 — Contain: open a vuln-mgmt ticket with the owner mandating upgrade to >=6.7.22 (v6 line) or >=7.0.0-rc12 (v7 line); as a temporary workaround, instruct the owner to set `shouldSyncHistoryMessage: () => false` in socket config and drop `messages.upsert` events containing a `requestId` field. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot on the application's process accountName / install path to inventory every host that runs the same Node.js service; check if the service is internet-exposed (sees WhatsApp WebSocket traffic) versus an internal-only deployment, and prioritise the externally-reachable instances.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "package.json"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\node_modules\baileys\", @"\node_modules\@whiskeysockets\baileys\", "/node_modules/baileys/", "/node_modules/@whiskeysockets/baileys/")
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), WriteCount=count(), arg_max(Timestamp, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName) by DeviceId, DeviceName, FolderPath
| project FirstSeen, LastSeen, DeviceName, FolderPath, WriteCount, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by LastSeen desc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where CveId =~ "CVE-2026-48063" or (SoftwareName has_any ("baileys", "@whiskeysockets/baileys"))
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Vulnerable Baileys WhatsApp Library package.json Write (CVE-2026-48063)
id: 7c0c4d2a-9b8e-4c1f-9b5f-2026480630a1
description: Detects creation or modification of package.json inside a node_modules/baileys or node_modules/@whiskeysockets/baileys directory, indicating an install of a library affected by CVE-2026-48063 (message.upsert / app-state spoofing) when version is < 6.7.22 or in the 7.0.0-rc.1 .. 7.0.0-rc11 range.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qvv5-jq5g-4cgg
  - https://github.com/WhiskeySockets/Baileys/commit/3beb08eecfcb4e65722e674034bd84fb11a9de35
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/18
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.001
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_baileys:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\node_modules\baileys\package.json'
      - '\node_modules\@whiskeysockets\baileys\package.json'
  condition: selection_baileys
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate developers building Node.js services that consume the Baileys WhatsApp library on a corporate workstation
  - CI build agents pulling node_modules during pipeline runs
level: low
@file.path:(*\\node_modules\\baileys\\package.json OR *\\node_modules\\@whiskeysockets\\baileys\\package.json OR */node_modules/baileys/package.json OR */node_modules/@whiskeysockets/baileys/package.json)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| regex("(/|\\\\)node_modules(/|\\\\)(@whiskeysockets(/|\\\\))?baileys(/|\\\\)package\\.json$", field=TargetFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName], function=[min(@timestamp, as=FirstSeen), max(@timestamp, as=LastSeen), count(as=Writes)])
| sort(LastSeen, order=desc)

Baileys CVE-2026-48063 vulnerable version on Defender TVM inventory AIWeaponization High
Direct vulnerability-management lookup for any device Defender TVM reports as running a Baileys WhatsApp library version covered by CVE-2026-48063. Complements the file-event UC by pivoting on the CVE ID where Defender's vulnerability catalog has ingested the GHSA. Rationale: Uses the exact CVE ID from the GHSA (CVE-2026-48063) and the published affected packages (npm:baileys, npm:@whiskeysockets/baileys). Joins DeviceInfo to enrich with IsInternetFacing so vuln-mgmt can prioritise hosts whose Node.js service is exposed (the spoofing requires a remote peer to reach the WhatsApp socket). No Splunk/Sigma/Datadog/Falcon equivalents — Defender TVM is the unique data source. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/WhiskeySockets/Baileys/commit/3beb08eecfcb4e65722e674034bd84fb11a9de35

  • Application owners already on the patched commit but TVM not yet refreshed (TVM catalog can lag by hours)
  • Dev-only laptops where Baileys is installed for evaluation but never connected to a WhatsApp session — vulnerable on paper, not exploitable in practice
  • Air-gapped or internal-only Node.js services that cannot receive a malicious protocolMessage from an external peer
  • Container images cached on host disk where the running container has already been replaced with a patched image
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: rank the result set by IsInternetFacing=true and confirm each device actually runs a long-lived Node.js service consuming Baileys (`Get-Process node` / `tasklist /svc`), not just a leftover node_modules tree. Step 2 — Contain: for confirmed-vulnerable internet-facing services, open a P1 patch ticket forcing upgrade to baileys >=6.7.22 or >=7.0.0-rc12, and have the owner deploy the article's workaround (drop messages.upsert events with a `requestId` field and set `shouldSyncHistoryMessage: () => false`) while the patch is rolled out. Step 3 — Hunt: cross-reference with the file-event UC to catch hosts running vulnerable Baileys that TVM has not yet catalogued; pivot on the service's outbound WebSocket destinations to identify which WhatsApp accounts are exposed.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where CveId =~ "CVE-2026-48063"
   or (SoftwareVendor has_any ("whiskeysockets", "baileys") and SoftwareName has "baileys")
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, OSPlatform, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP, LoggedOnUsers) by DeviceId
) on DeviceId
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, OSPlatform, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate, LoggedOnUsers
| order by IsInternetFacing desc, Timestamp desc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where CveId =~ "CVE-2026-48063"
   or (SoftwareVendor has_any ("whiskeysockets", "baileys") and SoftwareName has "baileys")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766") or SHA1 in~ ("2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766") or MD5 in~ ("2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766") or SHA1 in~ ("2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766") or MD5 in~ ("2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Vulnerable go-base deployment: AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random in process command-line AIInstallation High
Hunts for processes launched with the hardcoded weak JWT signing key from CVE-2026-48031 (dhax/go-base). Any service started with AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random is trivially exploitable — an attacker reading the public repo can forge admin JWTs in seconds. Surfaces the vulnerable deployment before exploitation occurs. Rationale: Pivots on the exact literal string from dev.env:10 and cmd/serve.go:35 — the article explicitly states this is the hardcoded default that ships to all users. Process command-lines capture both the env-var prefix form (AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random env -- ./serve) and Viper-resolved dump output. Corroborated via the linked fix PR #31 which removes exactly this string. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mqq6-462x-jxmm • https://github.com/dhax/go-base/pull/31
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1078
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer running the unpatched boilerplate on a workstation while learning the framework
  • CI/CD job for the go-base reference app intentionally exercising the vulnerable path
  • Security researcher reproducing CVE-2026-48031 in an isolated lab
  • Internal CTF / training environment using the boilerplate as a teaching artifact
  • Stale containers from before the May 2026 patch still running in non-prod
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Users\" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !contains @"\dev\" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !contains @"\sandbox\" and DeviceName !has "-dev" and DeviceName !has "-lab"
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: confirm the host's role — is this a production API, staging, or a dev box? Pull the parent process chain to identify the orchestrator (systemd, kubelet, docker-compose). Check whether the binary path resolves to a go-base derivative (`go-base`, `serve`, project name in folder path). 2) CONTAIN: if production or internet-facing, stop the service immediately; rotate AUTH_JWT_SECRET to `openssl rand -base64 32`; invalidate all existing tokens server-side. If still dev, file a vuln ticket and gate deployment. 3) HUNT: scan all hosts for the same string; pivot to web access logs for the affected service and run UC2/UC3 against the same window to determine whether forgery attempts already landed; check git history for any internal forks of dhax/go-base still pinned below the PR#31 commit.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random"
    or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath,
          ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (SecurityEvent
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where EventID == 4688
   | where CommandLine has "AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random"
   | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = SubjectUserName,
             Process = NewProcessName, CommandLine,
             ParentProcess = ParentProcessName),
  (ImProcessCreate
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random"
        or ParentProcessCommandLine has "AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random"
   | project TimeGenerated, Computer = DvcHostname, Account = ActorUsername,
             Process = ActingProcessName, CommandLine = ActingProcessCommandLine,
             ParentProcess = ParentProcessName)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

description: Detects services launched with the AUTH_JWT_SECRET environment variable set to the hardcoded default 'random' shipped by github.com/dhax/go-base prior to PR#31. Per CVE-2026-48031 the secret is public, allowing trivial JWT forgery against any reachable API.

  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mqq6-462x-jxmm
  - https://github.com/dhax/go-base/pull/31
author: Detection Engineering

tags:

  - attack.t1078

  category: process_creation

Burst of JWT validation failures (401/403) on go-base /api/v1/* endpoints from single source AIExploitation Medium
Detects token-forgery probing against a go-base-style API: an attacker with the leaked 'random' secret will iterate JWT claims (sub, roles, exp) until validation passes. Each iteration that misses produces a 401 or 403 from the jwtauth middleware. A sustained burst from one source IP — especially against the article-named paths — is the failed-forgery footprint. Rationale: Anchored on the exact endpoint prefix /api/v1/ used in the article PoC. The 401/403 pair is what go-chi/jwtauth/v5 returns when signature verification fails or when the resolved roles don't satisfy the route's RequireRole — the two failure modes a forgery attacker iterates through. Threshold of 20 in 5m is empirical for noisy probing while staying above legitimate expired-token churn. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mqq6-462x-jxmm
ATT&CKT1606 T1110.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Mobile or SPA client with an expired refresh-token loop hammering /api/v1/me
  • Synthetic monitoring (Pingdom, Datadog Synthetics) probing the API without valid auth
  • Pen-test or DAST scanner (Burp, ZAP) run against the staging API
  • Misconfigured CI job using a stale JWT in its smoke test
  • Authenticated user crossing token-rotation window during a deploy
Suppression filter
| where UA !has "Pingdom" and UA !has "Datadog Synthetics" and UA !has "StatusCake" and UA !has "UptimeRobot"
| where not (UA has "python-requests" and Host has "-dev")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: pull the burst's full request set — are the 401/403s clustered on /api/v1/admin/* and /api/v1/token/refresh (PoC pattern) or scattered? Look at the User-Agent: legitimate clients are consistent; forgery probes often rotate or use `python-requests/*` matching the article PoC. 2) CONTAIN: WAF-block the source IP at the edge if non-corporate; if the host serves go-base, rotate AUTH_JWT_SECRET immediately and invalidate sessions. Run UC1 against the backing host to confirm whether it shipped with the hardcoded default. 3) HUNT: pivot to UC3 with the same source IP — if a 200 follows the burst on /api/v1/admin/*, treat as confirmed exploitation. Pull DB audit logs for any data accessed by the forged session.
let WindowMinutes = 5m;
let FailureThreshold = 20;
union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
   | where csUriStem startswith "/api/v1/"
   | where scStatus in (401, 403)
   | project TimeGenerated, SrcIp = cIP, Host = sSiteName, Uri = csUriStem,
             Status = scStatus, UA = csUserAgent, Method = csMethod),
  (AppServiceHTTPLogs
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
   | where CsUriStem startswith "/api/v1/"
   | where ScStatus in (401, 403)
   | project TimeGenerated, SrcIp = CIp, Host = CsHost, Uri = CsUriStem,
             Status = ScStatus, UA = UserAgent, Method = CsMethod),
  (CommonSecurityLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
   | where RequestURL has "/api/v1/"
   | where EventOutcome in ("401", "403")
   | project TimeGenerated, SrcIp = SourceIP, Host = DestinationHostName,
             Uri = RequestURL, Status = toint(EventOutcome),
             UA = RequestClientApplication, Method = RequestMethod)
| summarize FailedAttempts = count(),
            UniquePaths = dcount(Uri),
            SamplePaths = make_set(Uri, 8),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
            by SrcIp, Host, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMinutes)
| where FailedAttempts >= FailureThreshold
| order by LastSeen desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.status=401 OR Web.status=403) AND (Web.url="*/api/v1/*") by Web.src Web.dest Web.url _time span=5m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| stats sum(count) as Failures dc(url) as UniquePaths values(url) as Paths min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime by src dest
| where Failures >= 20
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| sort - Failures

| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| stats sum(count) as Failures dc(url) as UniquePaths values(url) as Paths min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime by src dest
| where Failures >= 20
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| sort - Failures
go-base admin/refresh endpoint hit without preceding successful login from same source AIActions on Objectives Medium
After an attacker forges a JWT with AUTH_JWT_SECRET='random', they skip the login flow entirely and hit /api/v1/admin/users or /api/v1/token/refresh directly. Legitimate users always traverse the login endpoint first. Surfaces successful forged-token use by anti-joining admin/refresh hits against recent successful logins from the same source IP. Rationale: The article PoC explicitly shows the attacker skipping the login step — `requests.get('/api/v1/admin/users')` and `requests.post('/api/v1/token/refresh')` with only a forged Authorization header. Anti-joining admin hits against logins on the same source IP catches exactly that footprint. Endpoints are the literal paths named in the PoC code block. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mqq6-462x-jxmm
ATT&CKT1550.001 T1078
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Service-to-service API client using a long-lived bearer token (no human login flow)
  • Mobile app resuming a stored refresh token after >30 minutes of inactivity
  • NAT egress IP where one user logged in and another reaches admin paths
  • API key / PAT auth that bypasses /login by design
  • SSO callback flow where the login endpoint sits on a different host than the API
Suppression filter
| where UA !has "okhttp" and UA !has "Darwin/" and UA !has "Android"
| where UA !has "GoogleHC" and UA !has "kube-probe"
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: pull the full request set for the source IP — does the UA / TLS fingerprint match a known mobile or service client? Check whether the AdminUri is /api/v1/admin/users specifically (the PoC path) versus a benign admin route. Validate against UC1 — was the backing host running with AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random? 2) CONTAIN: revoke the offending session/token at the API; if confirmed forged, rotate AUTH_JWT_SECRET to a 32-byte random value (`openssl rand -base64 32`) and force re-auth for all users. Block source IP at the WAF. 3) HUNT: search the DB / app audit logs for actions taken under the forged identity (the PoC creates an admin@example.com sub claim — look for any sub value not present in the user table). Pivot on UA across the org to find other IPs using the same forgery toolkit.
let LookbackHours = 2h;
let LoginWindowSec = 1800;
let AdminHits =
  union isfuzzy=true
    (W3CIISLog
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
     | where csUriStem startswith "/api/v1/admin/" or csUriStem matches regex @"^/api/v1/token/refresh"
     | where scStatus == 200
     | project AdminTime = TimeGenerated, SrcIp = cIP, AdminUri = csUriStem,
               UA = csUserAgent, Host = sSiteName),
    (AppServiceHTTPLogs
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
     | where CsUriStem startswith "/api/v1/admin/" or CsUriStem matches regex @"^/api/v1/token/refresh"
     | where ScStatus == 200
     | project AdminTime = TimeGenerated, SrcIp = CIp, AdminUri = CsUriStem,
               UA = UserAgent, Host = CsHost);
let LoginEvents =
  union isfuzzy=true
    (W3CIISLog
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours + 1h)
     | where csUriStem in ("/api/v1/login", "/api/v1/auth/login", "/login", "/oauth/token")
     | where scStatus == 200
     | project LoginTime = TimeGenerated, SrcIp = cIP),
    (AppServiceHTTPLogs
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours + 1h)
     | where CsUriStem in ("/api/v1/login", "/api/v1/auth/login", "/login", "/oauth/token")
     | where ScStatus == 200
     | project LoginTime = TimeGenerated, SrcIp = CIp);
AdminHits
| join kind=leftouter LoginEvents on SrcIp
| extend HasRecentLogin = isnotempty(LoginTime)
         and datetime_diff('second', AdminTime, LoginTime) between (0 .. LoginWindowSec)
| summarize HasRecentLogin = max(HasRecentLogin),
            AdminHits = dcount(AdminTime),
            Endpoints = make_set(AdminUri, 10),
            UAs = make_set(UA, 5),
            FirstHit = min(AdminTime),
            LastHit = max(AdminTime)
          by SrcIp, Host
| where HasRecentLogin == false
| order by LastHit desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.status=200 AND (Web.url="*/api/v1/admin/*" OR Web.url="*/api/v1/token/refresh*") by Web.src Web.url _time
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename _time as admin_time
| join type=left src [
    | tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.status=200 AND (Web.url="*/api/v1/login*" OR Web.url="*/api/v1/auth/login*" OR Web.url="*/login*" OR Web.url="*/oauth/token*") by Web.src _time
    | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
    | stats max(_time) as last_login by src ]
| where isnull(last_login) OR (admin_time - last_login) > 1800
| eval login_gap_min = round((admin_time - coalesce(last_login,0))/60, 1)
| table admin_time src url login_gap_min last_login
| sort - admin_time
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.status=200 AND (Web.url="*/api/v1/admin/*" OR Web.url="*/api/v1/token/refresh*") by Web.src Web.url _time
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename _time as admin_time
| join type=left src [
    | tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.status=200 AND (Web.url="*/api/v1/login*" OR Web.url="*/api/v1/auth/login*" OR Web.url="*/login*" OR Web.url="*/oauth/token*") by Web.src _time
    | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
    | stats max(_time) as last_login by src ]
| where isnull(last_login) OR (admin_time - last_login) > 1800
| eval login_gap_min = round((admin_time - coalesce(last_login,0))/60, 1)
| table admin_time src url login_gap_min last_login
| sort - admin_time
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High

ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-48031")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-48031")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-48031")

| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity

    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-48031")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve

Compromised Rust crate onering performs code exfiltration

Aikido
2026-06-10 8 use cases 3 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

The compromised onering Rust crate v1.4.1 on crates.io shipped a malicious build.rs that exfiltrates the diff of your latest commit to a hosted Sentry endpoint every time you build. Category: Vulnerabilities & Threats

ATT&CKT1176 T1190 T1195.002
Domainso4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] onering 1.4.1 crate landing in cargo registry cache (compromised-version install)
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound POST to onering crate C2 Sentry ingest endpoint (o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io) · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] curl POSTing Sentry envelope payload from cargo/build-script-build context · [LLM] Rust build script (build-script-build) executing 'git diff HEAD^ HEAD' for source-code harvesting · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
Outbound POST to onering crate C2 Sentry ingest endpoint (o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io) AICommand & Control High
Detects network connections from any process to the specific Sentry ingest endpoint used by the malicious onering 1.4.1 crate to exfiltrate git diffs. The domain/org/project ID combination is unique to this campaign and any contact from a development machine indicates compromised build pipeline. Rationale: Anchored on the article's exact IOCs: the full Sentry ingest hostname o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io, the project path /4511539669368912/envelope/, and the DSN public key 8197ee42c4f59c83f4cc6d48f5bae821. All three are unique to this attacker's tenant so contact = compromise — no need to baseline.
ATT&CKT1041 T1071.001 T1567
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal security researcher reproducing the malicious build.rs in a sandbox
  • Threat-intel platform actively fetching the URL for IOC enrichment
  • Aikido's own scanner crawling the endpoint during a customer demo
  • DFIR analyst manually testing the indicator from their workstation
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe")  // exclude browser-based research lookups
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "aikido" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "ioc-research"
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Identify the source host and the initiating process — confirm it's a developer workstation/CI runner and look for nearby cargo/rustc/build-script-build activity in DeviceProcessEvents within ±10 minutes of the network event. Pull the dev's Cargo.lock and grep for `onering = "1.4.1"`. 2) CONTAIN: Isolate the host, kill cargo/build processes, rotate any git credentials and SSH/PAT tokens stored on the box, force a fresh clone of every active repo. Treat the contents of the most recent commit diff on each affected repo as leaked. 3) HUNT: Across all dev/CI estate, run `Get-Content **/Cargo.lock | Select-String 'onering'`. Pivot on Sentry org id `o4511539639222272` for any related campaign infrastructure and check git log for any onering references in branch dependencies pulled from the GitHub mirror.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io"
   or RemoteUrl has "4511539669368912/envelope"
   or RemoteUrl has "8197ee42c4f59c83f4cc6d48f5bae821"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Url has_any ("o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io", "4511539669368912/envelope", "8197ee42c4f59c83f4cc6d48f5bae821")
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Url, HttpMethod, HttpUserAgent=HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, DstHostname
| union (
    ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DstHostname has "o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io"
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

curl POSTing Sentry envelope payload from cargo/build-script-build context AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the article's specific exfiltration shape: curl invoked with the malicious Sentry envelope URL and/or DSN, where the parent is a Rust build artifact (cargo, rustc, build-script-build). Catches the same exfil even if RemoteUrl is blocked at the proxy. Rationale: Pivots on three article-extracted strings that, together, can't be a coincidence: the exact ingest URL path 4511539669368912/envelope/, the DSN public key 8197ee42c4f59c83f4cc6d48f5bae821, and the unusual Content-Type application/x-sentry-envelope literally shown in the request() call. Catches the exfil even when DNS is sinkholed.
ATT&CKT1059 T1105 T1041
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal security testing reproducing the payload
  • Threat-intel automation probing the URL for liveness
  • DFIR analyst manually replaying the IOC
  • Aikido employee/customer testing the disclosed sample in a lab
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Pull the parent chain — look for cargo / rustc / build-script-build / cargo build / cargo check several hops up. If the grandparent is a build script, treat as confirmed onering. 2) CONTAIN: Kill cargo and any background rust-analyzer/cargo-watch processes, isolate host, revoke all git PATs and SSH keys present on the box. The diff of the last commit on every active repo on that host should be considered exfiltrated. 3) HUNT: Search `DeviceProcessEvents | where InitiatingProcessFileName startswith "build-script-build"` across the org for the last 30 days. Inventory Cargo.lock files for `onering` at any version and Cargo.toml files declaring it as a direct or transitive dependency.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("curl.exe","curl")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (
    "o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io",
    "4511539669368912/envelope",
    "8197ee42c4f59c83f4cc6d48f5bae821",
    "application/x-sentry-envelope"
  )
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentImage=InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentName=InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          GrandparentName=InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("curl.exe","/curl") or TargetProcessName has_any ("curl.exe","/curl")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (
    "o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io",
    "4511539669368912/envelope",
    "8197ee42c4f59c83f4cc6d48f5bae821",
    "application/x-sentry-envelope"
  )
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
